### findComponents

Ids of a mesh's vertices, edges or faces matching every predicate given (normal direction, side of the symmetry plane, box, distance, extreme along an axis, open border). Ids index the editable cage, like selectComponents. Changes nothing; see selectComponentsWhere to select them.

**Objects:** [mesh]

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `k` | str | `'face'` | vertex, edge or face. |
| `normal` | `n` | tuple[float, float, float] |  | Keep components whose normal is within angle of this direction (world space). |
| `angle` |  | float | `30.0` | Tolerance for normal=, degrees. |
| `side` | `s` | str |  | '+x', '-x', '+y', ... keeps components whose centre is on that side of the object-space origin plane; 'center' (or 'centerx', 'centery', 'centerz') keeps those on the plane. |
| `box` | `b` | list |  | [[minX, minY, minZ], [maxX, maxY, maxZ]], world space: keep components whose centre is inside. None leaves that side open, so [[None, 20, None], [None, None, None]] is everything above y=20. |
| `direction` | `dir` | tuple[float, float, float] |  | Edges only: keep edges running along this world direction (either way) within angle; (0, 1, 0) finds vertical edges, whose ring polyInsertLoop cuts with a horizontal loop. |
| `near` |  | tuple[float, float, float] |  | World point; with radius= keeps components within it, else keeps the count nearest. |
| `radius` | `r` | float |  | Distance for near=, cm. |
| `extreme` | `x` | str |  | '+y', '-z', ...: keep the count components furthest along that world direction (the top face is extreme='+y'). |
| `count` | `c` | int | `1` | How many to keep for extreme= or near= without radius. |
| `border` |  | bool |  | True keeps only components on an open border, False only interior ones. |
| `shell` |  | int |  | Keep components of one connected shell: 0 is the largest, numbered as meshCheck lists them. |
| `fromSelection` | `fs` | bool | `False` | Only consider the currently selected components of that kind. |
| `tolerance` | `t` | float |  | Distance counted as on a plane for side=, cm (default scales with the mesh). |

### flowAlongSurface

Flow meshes onto a surface with a live surfaceFlow modifier (FlowAlongSrf): each mesh's XZ footprint maps onto the surface's UV rectangle, or onto a rectangular patch of quads (selected faces, parametrization grid), and its height (Y) follows the surface normal. Select the meshes, then the surface last. Returns the modifiers.

**Objects:** meshes

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `parametrization` |  | str |  | How surface positions are found: the surface's UVs, or the rows and columns of a rectangular patch of quads (targetFaces). One of `uv`, `grid`. |
| `uvSet` |  | str |  | UV set to map through (uv parametrization); empty is uv0. |
| `uMin` |  | float |  | Start of the coordinate range the mesh's X extent maps onto. |
| `vMin` |  | float |  | Start of the coordinate range the mesh's Z extent maps onto (Z runs against V). |
| `uMax` |  | float |  | End of the U range. |
| `vMax` |  | float |  | End of the V range. |
| `swapUV` |  | bool |  | Map X to V and Z to U. |
| `heightScale` |  | float |  | Height off the surface per unit of the mesh's Y. |
| `heightBase` |  | str |  | Measure height from Y = 0 (the construction plane) or from the mesh's lowest point. One of `origin`, `bottom`. |
| `envelope` |  | float |  | How much of the flow applies, 0 to 1. |
| `target` | `t` | str |  | The surface mesh; else the last selected mesh. |
| `faces` |  | list |  | Surface faces to flow onto; else its selected faces, else all of it. |

```python
lila.ops.flowAlongSurface("Logo", target="Hull")
```

### freezeTransforms

Bake translate/rotate/scale into mesh or curve points, leaving identity values. World positions don't change. With hierarchy (the default, like Maya) everything parented under the objects is frozen too; without it the children's transforms absorb what their parent gives up. Joints keep their translate and take their rotation into jointOrient, or with jointOrient line up with the world.

**Objects:** objects

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `translate` |  | bool | `True` | Freeze translation. |

### fullBodyIk

Pose a whole skeleton so each pinned joint reaches its target. The motion spreads over the joints between the pins and the hips by stiffness; everything else keeps its pose. Writes the joints' rotate (and the hips' translate) as FK. Returns {'error': the largest pin miss in cm}.

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pins` | `p` | list |  | [{'joint': name, 'position': [x, y, z], 'rotation': [x, y, z], 'weight': 1.0}], world space; rotation is XYZ Euler degrees. position and rotation are each optional. |
| `hold` | `h` | list |  | Joints pinned where they are now (position and rotation). |
| `root` | `r` | str |  | Top joint of the skeleton to solve; default the first pin's top joint. |
| `stiffness` | `st` | Any |  | {joint: 0..1}: how much each joint resists turning, so its neighbours take the motion. |
| `moveRoot` | `mr` | bool | `True` | Let the hips move when turning joints is not enough. |
| `key` | `k` | bool | `False` | Key the posed joints. |
| `autoPose` | `ap` | bool | `False` | Let the auto-poser place the unpinned body, as a person would stand to reach the pins (UE5 Manny joint names). |

Build textured hair cards from curves with live history: one per curve, per clump, or per guide curve; width with a taper ramp, segments, facing the scalp or following the curve, twist, and UVs in random atlas cells. A card mesh per curve node. Returns [mesh, hairCards, ...].

| `width` |  | float |  | Card width at the root, cm. |
| `autoWidth` |  | bool |  | Size each clump or guide card to the spread of its curves. |
| `widthScale` |  | float |  | Scale of the automatic width. |
| `taper` |  | str |  | Width along the card: keys "t:scale", t from 0 at the root to 1 at the tip. |

| `widthSegments` |  | int |  | Quads across each card. |
| `facing` |  | str |  | Cards lie flat to the scalp, follow rotation minimising curve frames, or face the up vector. One of `surfaceNormal`, `curveFrame`, `upVector`. |
| `upVector` |  | tuple[float, float, float] |  | Up for facing = upVector, and without a scalp. |
| `tilt` |  | float |  | Turn of every card about its curve, degrees. |
| `twist` |  | float |  | Twist from root to tip, degrees. |
| `offset` |  | float |  | Lift off the scalp along the card's facing, cm. |
| `doubleSided` |  | bool |  | Give each card a back face. |

| `atlasRows` |  | int |  | Texture atlas cells down. |
| `variations` |  | int |  | Use only the first this many cells; 0 uses them all. |
| `seed` |  | int |  | Random seed for picking cells. |
| `flipU` |  | bool |  | Mirror each card's u. |
| `flipV` |  | bool |  | Root at the bottom of its cell instead of the top. |

| `guides` |  | list |  | Guide curves (sets source = guides). |

### hide

Hide objects (visibility off). Defaults to the selection.

### ikChain

Make an IK chain from a start joint to an end effector, solved by a base ikHandle. The joints keep their keyed rotate: grabbing the controller solves the chain and writes (keys) the rotations, and a locked key holds the controller until the chain's next key. Returns the chain.

**Objects:** startJoint endJoint

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `startJoint` | `sj` | str |  | First joint. |
| `endJoint` | `ej` | str |  | End effector. |
| `solver` | `sol` | str |  | IK solver; default ik2BoneSolver for three joints, else FABRIK. |
| `name` | `n` | str |  | Chain name; default <effector>_ik. |
| `poleVector` | `pv` | tuple[float, float, float] |  | Bend direction from the start joint; default the chain's current bend. |
| `parent` | `p` | str |  | Node to put the element under, such as a character. |

### ikHandle

Create an IK handle that solves the chain from startJoint down to endEffector (or the first and last selected joints); the handle starts on the end joint, so nothing moves. The joints keep their keyable rotate as FK and the handle's ikBlend crossfades to the solution. With refresh=True, re-reads the rest layout of the given handles' chains after joints were edited. Returns the handle.

**Objects:** handles (refresh only)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `startJoint` | `sj` | str |  | First joint of the chain. |
| `endEffector` | `ee` | str |  | Last joint of the chain; the one placed on the handle. |
| `solver` | `sol` | str |  | IK solver id; empty picks ik2BoneSolver for three joints, else ikFabrikSolver. |
| `name` | `n` | str |  | Handle name. |
| `poleVector` | `pv` | tuple[float, float, float] |  | Bend direction from the start joint; defaults to the chain's current bend. |
| `poleAngle` | `pa` | float |  | Roll of the bend plane, degrees. |
| `refresh` | `rf` | bool | `False` | Re-read the rest layout of the given handles' chains. |

### ikLock

Lock (plant) or unlock the key at a time on IK and reverse foot controllers: a locked key holds the controller where it is, and the solver holds the hand or foot there, until the chain's next key. Toggles without state. Returns each chain's new state.

**Objects:** IK chains, their controllers or joints in them

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `time` | `t` | float |  | Seconds; default the current time. |
| `state` | `s` | bool |  | Locked or not; default the opposite of now. |

### ikMatch

Put IK controllers (and their poles) onto the joints' current pose, which grabbing one also does. Returns the chains.

**Objects:** IK chains, their controllers or joints in them

### ikPole

Swing IK chains' pole by degrees (the knee or elbow turns around the line from hip to foot), posing the joints. turn also turns the controller with it, so the foot or hand follows the knee or elbow.

| `turn` | `tu` | bool | `False` | Turn the controller with the pole. |

### ikPose

Put IK controllers at a world position and rotation (or move and turn them by an amount) and pose their chains' joints there, keyed when the chain is animated. Returns the chains.

### importFbx

Import an FBX file: its node hierarchy as transforms, joints and meshes, converted to the scene's axes and cm. LimbNodes become joints (PreRotation into jointOrient), skins become skinClusters with the file's weights and bind matrices, morph channels become a morph with a target per channel (in-betweens kept), and one take is baked onto the channels. Cameras become camera nodes with their lens, film back and clipping (focal length, film back and clipping curves keyed per frame); lights are reported, not imported. Returns the new node names, or with report=True a dict of nodes, roots, joints, skinClusters, take, fps, skipped and warnings.

**Objects:** path

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `parent` | `p` | str |  | Parent the imported roots under this node. |
| `skins` |  | bool | `True` | Rebuild skins as joints and skinClusters with their weights and bind pose. |
| `animation` | `anim` | bool | `True` | Bake the take onto translate/rotate/scale, one key per frame. |
| `take` |  | str |  | AnimStack to import; the file's active one (or first) by default. |
| `setPlayback` |  | bool | `True` | Set the scene fps and playback range from the take. |
| `instances` |  | bool | `True` | Objects sharing one geometry come in as instances of the first. |
| `report` |  | bool | `False` | Return the import report instead of just the names. |
| `select` |  | bool | `True` | Select the imported roots. |

Not undoable.

### importGltf

Import a glTF 2.0 file (.gltf with its .bin and images, embedded data URIs, or binary .glb): the default scene's nodes as transforms, joints, meshes and cameras, converted from glTF's Y-up metres to the scene's axes and cm.

Each mesh becomes one Lila mesh, its primitives becoming material slots, with normals (hard edges where they split), tangents, every UV set (flipped to Lila's V-up) and every vertex color set; vertices split for seams weld back into points. Skins become skinClusters on joints with every JOINTS_n/WEIGHTS_n influence and the inverse bind matrices; a joint's rest rotation goes into its jointOrient. Morph targets become a morph with their names and default weights. Animation channels become curves: LINEAR and STEP keys exactly, CUBICSPLINE with its tangents (rotations sampled every frame); with several animations each becomes a take, the first active. Cameras keep their field of view and clipping.

Materials become material nodes: base color and alpha mode, metallic and roughness (packed into an ORM map, written as a new image when the file's layout differs), occlusion, emissive with KHR_materials_emissive_strength, normal map (kept OpenGL style), double sided, KHR_materials_ior/specular as specular, KHR_texture_transform baked into the UVs, KHR_materials_unlit as the unlit shading model, and each texture's sampler as its map's wrap and filter. Embedded and converted images are written to textureDir. KHR_mesh_quantization, sparse accessors, EXT_meshopt_compression and KHR_draco_mesh_compression are decoded (a Draco primitive that fails to decode falls back to its uncompressed data when the file has it). KHR_lights_punctual lights come in as lights, intensity in candela or lux.

Returns the new node names, or with report=True a dict of nodes, roots, joints, skinClusters, cameras, lights, morphs, materials, images, takes, take, fps, start, end, curves, skipped, warnings and errors.

**Objects:** path

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `parent` | `p` | str |  | Parent the imported roots under this node. |
| `skins` |  | bool | `True` | Rebuild skins as joints and skinClusters with their weights and bind matrices. |
| `animation` | `anim` | bool | `True` | Import the animations as curves. |
| `take` |  | str |  | Import only this animation, by name or index; every animation by default. |
| `setPlayback` |  | bool | `True` | Set the scene fps and playback range from the (first) animation. |
| `materials` |  | bool | `True` | Create material nodes; off keeps only the slot names on the faces. |
| `textureDir` |  | str |  | Folder for embedded and converted images; <file folder>/<file name>_textures by default. |
| `report` |  | bool | `False` | Return the import report instead of just the names. |
| `select` |  | bool | `True` | Select the imported roots. |

### instance

Make instances of objects: meshes that share their source's mesh, so an edit to any of them changes all. Returns the new names.

reference=True makes references instead, which share the base mesh under the source's modifiers but keep a modifier stack of their own (same base, a different bevel).

**Objects:** objects

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `n` | str |  | Name for a single instance. |
| `reference` |  | bool | `False` | Share only the base mesh and keep a modifier stack of its own (same shape, a different bevel). Off, instances share the modifier stack too, so every copy looks the same and exports as one mesh. |

```python
instance("Bolt")
```

```python
instance("Panel", reference=True)
```

### lodGroup

Make an LOD group from objects (LOD0 first, in order), or edit the LOD group named. Returns the group's path.

With generate, LOD0 (one mesh) gets that many reduced copies as the next levels. Unreal imports the group as one mesh with these LODs.

**Objects:** objects (LOD0 first), or one lodGroup to edit

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `n` | str |  | Group name, and the base of the levels' names. Defaults to LOD0's name without any _LODn. |
| `screenSizes` | `ss` | Any |  | Unreal LOD screen size per level, like [1, 0.5, 0.25]; [] uses Unreal's automatic sizes. |
| `generate` | `g` | int | `0` | Reduced copies of LOD0 to add as further levels. |
| `ratio` | `r` | float | `0.5` | Triangles each generated level keeps of the one before, 0 to 1. |
| `autoName` | `an` | bool |  | Rename the levels <name>_LOD0, <name>_LOD1, ... On by default when creating. |

```python
lodGroup("Rock_LOD0", "Rock_LOD1", "Rock_LOD2", screenSizes=[1, 0.4, 0.15])
```

```python
lodGroup("Rock", generate=3, ratio=0.5)
```

### materialLint

Check a material's values against physical ranges: a texture set, a library id or a .lilamat path, evaluated small. Checks albedo (dielectrics 30 to 240 sRGB), pure black/white, metal reflectance (per metal), binary metallic, roughness, normal validity and convention, height range and tile seams; stylised materials relax the albedo checks. fix=True clamps what it can with Levels nodes (sets undoably, user/workspace files in place). all=True checks every library material (tier= to narrow). Returns {passed, failures, warnings, checks}.

**Objects:** material

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fix` |  | bool | `False` | Clamp what failed with Levels nodes. |
| `size` |  | int | `256` | Evaluation size, px. |
| `backend` |  | str |  | gpu or cpu (default: the GPU when there is one). |
| `physical` |  | str |  | Override the meta's physical category. One of `metal`, `dielectric`, `organic`, `emissive`, `stylised`. |
| `all` |  | bool | `False` | Every library material. |
| `tier` |  | str |  | With all: only this tier. |

### mayaConvert

Convert Maya files to Lila scenes: a file to a .lila / .lilaa, or every .ma / .mb in a folder. Each file is opened as its own scene and saved; the scene is left empty afterwards. Returns one entry per file with its destination (or error), skipped features and warnings.

**Objects:** source

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `source` | `src` | str |  | A .ma / .mb file, or a folder of them. |
| `destination` | `dst` | str |  | The .lila / .lilaa file, or a folder for folder mode; next to the source by default. |
| `format` |  | str | `'binary'` | binary (.lila) or ascii (.lilaa) when the destination is a folder. |
| `recursive` | `r` | bool | `False` | Folder mode: also convert files in subfolders (mirrored under the destination). |
| `overwrite` |  | bool | `True` | Replace existing destination files. |
| `force` | `f` | bool | `False` | Discard unsaved changes in the current scene. |
| `namespace` | `ns` | str |  | Put every imported name in this namespace. |
| `upAxis` |  | str | `'auto'` | auto (from Maya's default cameras), y or z: the file's up axis. |
| `skins` |  | bool | `True` | Rebuild skinClusters with their weights and bind matrices. |
| `morphs` |  | bool | `True` | Rebuild blendShapes as morphs, with their weight curves and set driven keys. |
| `animation` | `anim` | bool | `True` | Import animation curves on translate, rotate and scale. |
| `materials` |  | bool | `True` | Create materials from shading groups and assign them per face. |
| `references` |  | Any | `'reference'` | reference: referenced Maya / FBX / OBJ files become Lila references (Maya and FBX ones converted to a .lila beside them) with the scene's reference edits as overrides; import: their nodes as ordinary scene nodes; none: skip them. |
| `history` |  | bool | `True` | Keep a lone primitive creator (polyCube ...) as a live generator node. |
| `setPlayback` |  | bool | `True` | Set the scene fps and playback range from the file. |

Not undoable.

### measureSelection

Measure the selection without making nodes: 2 vertices or objects give distance and dx/dy/dz, 3 an angle, edges total and per-edge length, a closed edge loop or 4+ vertices a best-fit circle, faces area and perimeter, one object its bounding box (and diameter when it is cylinder-like), a measure node its value. Not undoable.

| `pitch` |  | float |  | Perspective elevation, degrees (negative looks down). |

### meshRepair

Find or fix broken geometry. mode='select' selects what each enabled check finds and reports the counts; mode='repair' fixes it: welds coincident points, collapses zero-length edges, drops lamina copies, merges zero-area slivers into a neighbour, splits non-manifold edges and vertices apart, fills holes, cuts n-gons and concave faces into quads and triangles, conforms winding, removes loose points and edges.

**Objects:** objects

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` |  | str | `'repair'` | select: select the problems instead of fixing them. Points, edges and faces are each selected in their own component mode, and the mode switches to whichever kind has the most; the log lists the counts per check. repair: fix them. |
| `coincident` |  | bool | `True` | Points closer than the tolerance to another (repair welds them). |
| `zeroLengthEdges` |  | bool | `True` | Edges shorter than the tolerance (repair collapses them). |
| `lamina` |  | bool | `True` | Faces built on exactly the points of another face (repair deletes the extra copy). |
| `zeroAreaFaces` |  | bool | `True` | Faces thinner than the tolerance (repair merges each into the face across its longest edge). |
| `nonManifoldEdges` |  | bool | `True` | Edges shared by three or more faces (repair splits the extra faces off). |
| `nonManifoldVertices` |  | bool | `True` | Vertices where separate fans of faces meet, like a bowtie (repair gives each fan its own vertex). |
| `holes` |  | bool | `False` | Edges on an open border (repair fills each hole with a face). Off by default: open meshes are often meant to be. |
| `ngons` |  | bool | `False` | Faces with more than four sides (repair triangulates them and joins the triangles back into convex quads where they fit). |
| `concave` |  | bool | `False` | Faces with a corner bending inward (repair cuts them into convex quads and triangles). |
| `zeroAreaUvs` |  | bool | `False` | Faces with no area in the first uv set. Repair only reports them: they need a new unwrap. |
| `flippedNormals` |  | bool | `True` | Faces wound against the rest of their shell, or closed shells facing inward (repair turns them). |
| `tolerance` |  | float | `-1.0` | Distance under which points coincide and edges and faces count as zero size, cm; negative scales with the mesh. |
| `removeLoose` |  | bool | `True` | Repair also removes points and edges left without faces. |

| `layer` |  | int |  | Work on this painted layer of the field the deformer reads (or of the field named). |
| `mesh` |  | str |  | For a field's painted layer: the mesh it is painted on. |

Mirror a joint hierarchy across a plane through the world origin. behavior=True mirrors the axes so equal rotations make mirrored poses; False keeps world orientation. Names swap searchReplace; side labels swap left/right. Returns the new joints.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `axis` | `ax` | str | `'x'` | Mirror across this axis: x mirrors across the YZ plane. |
| `behavior` | `b` | bool | `True` | Mirror behavior instead of orientation. |
| `searchReplace` | `sr` | list | `['_l', '_r']` | [search, replace] for the new names. |

### mirrorMorphTarget

Mirror a target through the base's symmetry (points matched across the axis plane in object space). mode flip makes a new target with the shape on the other side, named with left and right swapped; symmetrize copies one side onto the other in place. In-betweens go along. Returns the target written.

**Objects:** target

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `axis` |  | str | `'x'` | Mirror axis, object space. One of `x`, `y`, `z`. |

### move

Move objects. move(by=(x, y, z)) moves relative in `space`; move(to=(x, y, z)) puts each pivot at a world position. A selected parent and child move once.

move(x=0) sets one world axis and leaves the others: each selected object's pivot, or with components selected every selected point, so move(x=0) puts an edge loop on the centre line.

| `y` |  | float |  | World Y, cm. |
| `z` |  | float |  | World Z, cm. |
| `space` |  | str | `'world'` | 'world', 'object' or 'parent' for `by`. |

### moveComponents

Move the selected components by an offset in world space, or with normal= push each point along its own vertex normal (a face selection uses only the selected faces' normals, so the region inflates as a whole). uvn= also slides each point along its own surface tangents: U follows the uv0 u direction where the mesh has uvs (in edge mode, the selected edges), else the world axis least aligned with the selection's normal, and V completes the frame. Curve points use the curve's frame: U its tangent (a handle's own direction), N across it within its plane, V out of the plane.

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `by` |  | tuple[float, float, float] |  | Offset, cm. |
| `normal` |  | float |  | Distance along the vertex normals, cm. |
| `uvn` |  | tuple[float, float, float] |  | Distances along each point's own U tangent, V tangent and normal, cm. |
| `onto` |  | list |  | Meshes whose surface each moved point then lands on, at its closest point. |

### multiBoxBounds

Split each mesh at or under the selection into chunks that largely conform to boxes and create one collision shape per chunk, named UCX_<mesh>_01, _02 and so on and parented under the mesh. The mesh is voxelized (open and overlapping shells work), merged into regions, refit with minimum-volume boxes and split or merged until each chunk is full enough, never exceeding maxBoxes. Every point of the mesh lies inside some shape. With preview, nothing is created and the boxes come back as JSON. Returns the new meshes with the box count, average fill and coverage.

**Objects:** objects

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `maxBoxes` | `mb` | int | `8` | Most shapes per mesh. |
| `minFill` | `mf` | float | `0.85` | Occupied volume over box volume a chunk should reach before it stops being split and may be merged. |
| `minBoxSize` | `ms` | float | `0.0` | Smallest extent a split may leave, cm; 0 is two voxels. |
| `resolution` | `res` | int | `48` | Voxels along the longest side of the mesh. |
| `oriented` | `or` | bool | `True` | Fit each chunk with its own minimum-volume frame; off keeps every box on the world axes. |
| `padding` | `pd` | float | `0.0` | Pushed out on every side of each shape, cm. |
| `shape` | `s` | str | `'auto'` | box, hull, or auto (a box unless the chunk's convex hull is clearly smaller). |
| `maxHullPoints` | `mh` | int | `32` | Most points a hull keeps. |
| `preview` | `pv` | bool | `False` | Create nothing and return the boxes as JSON. |
| `nameFromSelection` | `ns` | bool | `True` | Name after the mesh it wraps, so Unreal pairs the shapes as that mesh's collision. |
| `name` | `n` | str | `'Collision'` | Base name when not named from the selection. |
| `prefix` | `p` | str | `'UCX_'` | Put before the name. |
| `parent` | `pa` | bool | `True` | Parent under the mesh it wraps, keeping it in place. |
| `generator` | `g` | bool | `False` | Keep each box's polyCube generator so its size stays editable. |

| `check` | `c` | bool | `False` | Return [[node, expectedName], ...] for names that break the rules. |
| `fix` | `f` | bool | `False` | Rename every node that breaks the rules. |

### orientPivot

Aim the pivot from the first picked component to the second, or along a single one.

The component selection splits into connected pieces (two edge loops are two pieces); with exactly two components picked, each is its own piece. With several pieces the aim runs from the first picked piece's centre to the last's. One piece aims along itself: a face or face region along its normal (up from the first face's longest edge), an edge from its first point to its second (up from its faces' normal), a closed loop through its plane (up toward its first picked point), an open chain from the end nearer the first pick to the other, a vertex along its normal (up along its longest edge).

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `aim` |  | str | `'x'` | Pivot axis that points along the aim. One of `x`, `-x`, `y`, `-y`, `z`, `-z`. |
| `up` |  | str | `'y'` | Pivot axis that points toward the up reference. One of `x`, `-x`, `y`, `-y`, `z`, `-z`. |
| `upReference` |  | str | `'component'` | What the up axis leans toward: the selection's own up (component), worldUp (world), or the object's own matching axis (object). Falls back to the others where it lines up with the aim. |
| `worldUp` |  | tuple[float, float, float] |  | Up direction for upReference='world'; the scene up when left out. |
| `position` |  | str | `'first'` | Where the pivot goes: the first picked piece's centre (first), the centre of everything selected (center), or where it is (keep). |
| `mode` |  | str | `'transform'` | transform: turn and move the object itself onto the aim, the mesh moved back so it stays put (undoes a freeze's lost rotation), so Object space then works along it. pivot: orient the object's pivot, leaving object and mesh alone. manipulator: pin only the component manipulator's axes, through selection changes, until resetComponentPivot. |

```python
orientPivot()  # two verts picked: the object turns so its X aims from the first to the second
```

```python
orientPivot(mode='manipulator')  # pin the component manipulator's axes instead
```

### parent

parent(child..., parent), or parent(child..., world=True). Keeps world transforms unless relative=True. chain=True parents each object under the next one, in order: (a, b, c) puts a under b and b under c. index=N places the objects, in order, at position N among the parent's children (0 is first), which also reorders objects already under that parent. Leaves the moved objects selected.

| `chain` | `ch` | bool | `False` | Parent in selection order, each under the next. |
| `index` | `i` | int |  | Position among the parent's children, counted without the moved objects. |

### polyBoolean

Union, difference or intersection of meshes (Manifold: robust, watertight output), with the seam cleaned up: slivers welded, the n-gons along the cut split into quads that carry on the edge loops, an optional rounded fillet, and weighted normals. The first object keeps the result; the others are deleted unless keepCutters=True.

**Objects:** base cutters...

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `operation` |  | str | `'difference'` | union, difference or intersection. |
| `keepCutters` |  | bool | `False` | Keep the cutter objects (hidden). |
| `live` |  | bool | `False` | Keep it live instead of baking: a boolean modifier per cutter, so moving or editing a cutter updates the cut. The cutters go in a template display layer (BooleanCutters): grey wire you select from the outliner. |
| `cleanup` |  | bool | `True` | Weld slivers and stray points along the seam. |
| `snapDistance` |  | float | `-1.0` | Weld distance for cleanup, cm; negative is a tenth of the median seam edge. |
| `splitNgons` |  | bool | `True` | Cut the n-gons along the seam into quads (and triangles) that carry on the edge loops. |
| `quadBand` |  | bool | `False` | Remesh a band of faces around the seam into quads that follow it, welded back into the faces around it. Falls back to splitting n-gons where the band's border can't be kept. |
| `bandRings` |  | int | `1` | Rings of faces past the seam the quad band takes in. |
| `timeout` |  | float | `5.0` | Seconds the quad band remesh may take before the n-gon split runs instead; 0 waits forever. |
| `filletWidth` |  | float | `0.0` | Width of a rounded strip along the seam, cm; 0 keeps it sharp. |
| `filletSegments` |  | int | `2` | Rows of faces across the fillet. |
| `hardAngle` |  | float | `30.0` | New edges sharper than this many degrees are marked hard. |
| `weightedNormals` |  | bool | `True` | Add a weighted normals modifier, if the mesh has none, so the n-gons shade flat. |

### polyCircularize

Fit the selected edge loops, the border of each selected face region, or the selected vertices to a circle in their best-fit plane, turned to move the points least. Points inside a face region follow the border smoothly, so a rectangular face comes out round, ready to extrude into a pipe. Open chains become an arc between their ends.

| `strength` |  | float | `1.0` | How far toward the shape, 0 to 1; soft selection fades it further. |

### polyConformToObject

Conform the selected components onto another mesh or a curve. loop: each selected edge loop (or face region border) lands one to one on the target's nearest closed loop (a cylinder's rim, a ring), at the turn that moves it least, or spread along it when the counts differ; face interiors follow. surface: every point to the nearest surface point. vertex: every point to the nearest target vertex. A curve target works through its line: loop spreads a loop along a closed curve, surface puts each point on the nearest point of the curve.

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `target` |  | str |  | Mesh or curve to conform to; default: the selected mesh or curve that has no components selected. |
| `mode` |  | str | `'loop'` | loop, surface or vertex. |
| `spacing` |  | str | `'even'` | Loop mode with unequal counts: even, keep or project. |
| `strength` |  | float | `1.0` | How far toward the shape, 0 to 1; soft selection fades it further. |

Move the selected edge loops onto the curvature of the surface around them (Maya's Edit Edge Flow). Each vertex lands on a curve through the nearest unselected vertices across the loop, shaped by the vertices beyond them, and neighbouring selected loops spread evenly between those, as subdividing would place them. Selected vertices off any chain, and face selections, fit both directions across each vertex.

| `tension` |  | float | `0.0` | Toward 1 flattens the curve, negative makes it fuller. |
| `loopSmooth` |  | float | `0.0` | Also smooth each loop along its length, 0 to 1, keeping its spacing. |

| `distance` | `d` | float | `1.0` | Inward distance, cm. |
| `depth` |  | float | `0.0` | Push of the inner faces along the normal, cm; the band ramps to it. |
| `planarAngle` |  | float | `1.0` | Degrees a region's faces may bend and still count as flat. |

### polyKnife

Knife / multi-cut: cut a mesh along a path of points, splitting the faces between them and the edges the path crosses. Between two points the cut follows the surface under the straight screen line joining them (seen from eye= or along direction=; without either, along the points' average normal). With loopEdge= it inserts an edge loop across that edge's quad ring instead, and with deleteEdge= it dissolves that edge. Follows the mesh's symmetry. Returns the new edges.

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mesh` |  | str |  | Mesh to cut; default: the selected or hilited mesh. |
| `points` |  | list |  | Path points: {"vertex": id}, {"edge": id, "t": 0..1 from its first point}, or {"face": id, "position": [x, y, z] world}. |
| `closed` |  | bool | `False` | Also cut from the last point back to the first. |
| `through` |  | bool | `False` | Cut every face under the line, hidden faces too. |
| `eye` |  | tuple[float, float, float] |  | World eye of a perspective view. |
| `direction` |  | tuple[float, float, float] |  | World view direction of an orthographic view. |
| `loopEdge` |  | int | `-1` | Insert an edge loop across this edge's ring instead of cutting a path. |
| `fraction` |  | float | `0.5` | Where along loopEdge the loop crosses it, from its first point. |
| `deleteEdge` |  | int | `-1` | Dissolve this edge, joining its two faces, instead of cutting. |
| `select` |  | bool | `True` | Select the new edges. |

### polyLockNormals

Store the current shading normals of the selected meshes as split normals, so later edits keep them.

### polyMerge

Weld selected vertices closer than a distance (all of a mesh's points if it has no component selection). Exactly two selected vertices weld whatever the distance.

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `distance` |  | float | `0.01` | Weld distance, cm. |
| `average` |  | bool | `False` | Move merged points to their average. |

### polyMergeCenter

Weld the selected vertices into one at their centre.

### polyMirror

Mirror whole meshes across the plane through the object's or the world's origin facing an axis, welding along the seam. direction positive keeps the + side and rebuilds the - side from it, cutting faces that cross the plane; negative does the reverse; both adds a mirrored copy of the whole mesh. flip=True reflects the mesh across the plane instead, keeping nothing of the original.

**Objects:** objects

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `axis` |  | str | `'x'` | x, y or z. |
| `direction` |  | str | `'positive'` | positive (+ to -), negative (- to +) or both. |
| `space` |  | str | `'object'` | object or world: whose origin and axes the plane uses. |
| `weld` |  | bool | `True` | Weld points on the plane. |
| `tolerance` |  | float | `0.001` | Points this close to the plane are cut onto it and welded, cm. |
| `flip` |  | bool | `False` | Reflect the mesh across the plane rather than adding a mirrored copy: the original is not kept. |

### polyOffsetLoop

Insert an edge loop either side of the selected edges, parallel to them (Maya's Offset Edge Loop). Partial loops end on a border, or inside the mesh by meeting at the end vertex or wrapping round it. Returns the new edges.

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `distance` |  | float | `0.25` | How far out: a fraction of each crossing edge's length, or cm with absolute. |
| `absolute` |  | bool | `False` | distance is in cm, square to the selected edges. |
| `side` |  | str | `'both'` | both, left or right of the edges' direction. |
| `ends` |  | str | `'converge'` | Open ends inside the mesh: converge (meet at the end vertex) or wrap (round it). |
| `deleteEdge` |  | bool | `False` | Dissolve the selected edges afterward, leaving the two new loops. |

### polyReduce

A mesh with modifiers gets a decimate modifier on top instead. Honours the mesh's symmetry: one half (or one radial wedge) is reduced and mirrored (or repeated).

### polySpherize

Push the selected components (whole meshes in object mode) onto a sphere fitted to them, or onto an ellipsoid with scale. center and radius override the fit (world space, cm); radiusMode picks the radius from the points otherwise. With alongNormals each point slides along its own normal to the sphere. Returns the sphere used: {center, radius, scale, rotation}, world space.

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |

| `radius` |  | float | `0.0` | Radius, cm; above 0 it replaces radiusMode. |
| `center` |  | tuple[float, float, float] |  | Sphere centre, world space cm; default: the fitted centre. |
| `scale` |  | tuple[float, float, float] | `[1.0, 1.0, 1.0]` | Ellipsoid semi-axis factors along its X, Y and Z. |
| `rotation` |  | tuple[float, float, float] | `[0.0, 0.0, 0.0]` | Turn of the ellipsoid's axes in world space, degrees (XYZ). |
| `alongNormals` |  | bool | `False` | Move each point along its own normal onto the sphere. |

### polyTriangulate

Triangulate the selected faces (the whole mesh in object mode), deterministically, as Unreal will. Concave and non-planar faces, collinear points and faces touching themselves split without overlaps or slivers, and no diagonal doubles an edge another face already has. With symmetry on, the mirrored faces split the mirrored way. A whole mesh with modifiers gets a triangulate modifier on top instead, so the result is triangulated rather than the cage.

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `beauty` |  | bool | `True` | Flip n-gon diagonals toward the largest smallest angle (what display and export use). |
| `quadSplit` |  | str | `'shortest'` | Quads split along the shorter diagonal (what display, export and MikkTSpace use) or always from the first corner. One of `shortest`, `first`. |

### polyUnlockNormals

Drop the stored split normals of the selected meshes, so shading comes from the hard and soft edges again.

### polyWeightedNormals

Face-weighted normals on the selected faces (whole meshes in object mode): each smooth fan takes the normal of its biggest faces, so chamfered or bevelled low poly shades its large faces flat and only the chamfers bend. Written as locked split normals, which export to FBX. polyUnlockNormals goes back to computed ones.

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | `m` | str | `'area'` | What weighs a face: area, angle (its corner angle) or areaAngle. |
| `dominance` | `d` | float | `0.5` | Faces under this fraction of the heaviest face in a fan are left out; 0 keeps all. |
| `keepSharp` | `ks` | bool | `True` | Keep hard edges split. |
| `faceStrength` | `fs` | bool | `True` | Only the faces with the highest face int faceStrength count, when the mesh has it. |

### quadRemesh

Auto quad remesh: a new all-quad mesh whose edge flow follows curvature, hard edges and guide curves, at about the target face count, with UVs (and optionally normals) transferred from the source. Open borders, sharp creases, crease corners and cone tips are kept. Where the shape is too thin or tight for the requested size (a strip narrower than the edge length) it retries finer, so the face count can come out higher. The kept source is hidden. Runs off the UI thread with a cancellable progress bar, and gives up after timeout= seconds with an error saying how far it got, changing nothing. Returns {name, metrics}.

**Objects:** source

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `targetFaces` |  | int | `500` | Approximate face count. |
| `timeout` |  | float | `5.0` | Seconds before giving up with an error saying how far it got, leaving the scene as it was; 0 waits forever. |
| `targetEdgeLength` |  | float | `0.0` | Edge length, cm; overrides targetFaces when positive. |
| `adaptivity` |  | float | `0.25` | 0 uniform, 1 much denser where curved; painted point 'density' multiplies. |
| `useHardEdges` |  | bool | `True` | Follow edges marked hard. |
| `sharpAngle` |  | float | `40.0` | Also follow creases sharper than this, degrees; negative disables. |
| `symmetry` |  | str | `'off'` | off, x, y or z: remesh half and mirror, exactly symmetric. |
| `guides` |  | list |  | Mesh nodes whose edges are guide curves. |
| `guidePoints` |  | list |  | Guide polylines as lists of world [x, y, z]. |
| `pureQuads` |  | bool | `True` | All quads; false allows a few triangles and pentagons. |
| `resolveGaps` |  | bool | `True` | Finer where the surface comes close to itself across a gap (a ball in a pocket), so the gap isn't bridged; costs faces. |
| `seamless` |  | bool | `False` | Experimental: also try a global layout that only turns at the poles, kept when it has fewer irregular points. |
| `poles` |  | list |  | The poles the edge flow turns at, as {position: world [x, y, z], valence: 3 or 5}, and nowhere else. Start from retopoPoles; on a closed shell (4 - valence) must sum to what retopoPoles reports. |
| `relaxIterations` |  | int | `6` | Tangential relax passes on the surface. |
| `transferUvs` |  | bool | `True` | Copy UV sets from the source. |
| `transferNormals` |  | bool | `False` | Copy the source's normals as custom normals. |
| `keepSource` |  | bool | `True` | Keep the source mesh; false deletes it. |
| `hideSource` |  | bool | `True` | Hide the kept source mesh. |
| `name` |  | str |  | Name of the new mesh. |

Not undoable.

### references

Every reference: namespace, path, loaded, and its local edits.

Not undoable.

### relaxMesh

Even out point spacing while keeping the form: points slide over the mesh's own starting surface (or a target mesh), points on sharp creases and hard edges slide only along them, and crease corners and cone tips stay. No face is allowed to fold over. Moves only the selected components when there is a component selection. Honours the mesh's symmetry.

**Objects:** objects

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `iterations` |  | int | `10` | Smoothing passes, 1 to 1000. |
| `strength` |  | float | `0.5` | Step toward the neighbour average per pass, 0 to 1. |
| `target` |  | str |  | Mesh to stay on; default is the mesh itself. |
| `project` |  | bool | `True` | Keep points on the surface. Off is plain smoothing, which shrinks and rounds the shape. |
| `pinBoundary` |  | bool | `True` | Keep border points fixed; off lets them slide along the border, keeping its outline. |
| `sharpAngle` |  | float | `12.0` | Edges whose faces meet sharper than this are creases that keep their line, degrees; negative turns it off. |
| `keepHardEdges` |  | bool | `True` | Hard edges keep their line like creases do. |
| `pinCreases` |  | bool | `False` | Keep points on creased edges fixed. |
| `pinHard` |  | bool | `False` | Keep points on hard edges fixed. |
| `pinSeams` |  | bool | `False` | Keep points on UV seams fixed. |

### reloadExtension

Unload and load an extension again from the same package, picking up changes.

**Objects:** id

Not undoable.

### reloadReference

Re-read a reference's file, keeping local edits. Clears undo.

**Objects:** namespace

Not undoable.

### relocateScene

Move the whole scene (or chosen hierarchies) so a point becomes the world origin, keeping every rig, deformer and animation working.

One rigid move M is applied: the roots take it through their channels and keys, and nodes that store world-space data (skin bind matrices, deformer bind matrices, world spaces, world up vectors, measures) are rewritten to match. Every transform and deformed mesh point is then checked at several frames (and in every take) against M times where it was; if anything is off by more than 1e-6 cm, or the scene holds a node type relocateScene doesn't know, nothing changes and the error says why. One undo step.

**Objects:** objects the from= point is taken from (default: the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `from` |  | str | `'bottom'` | The point that moves to `to`: bottom (the bottom centre of the objects' bounds), center (their bounds centre), pivot (the first object's pivot), components (the centre of the selected components), or an object's name (its pivot). Example: `relocateScene(from="Hero")` |
| `to` |  | tuple[float, float, float] |  | Where the from= point lands, cm. Default the world origin. |
| `offset` |  | tuple[float, float, float] |  | Move by this world offset instead of from= and to=, cm. Example: `relocateScene(offset=(-12000, 0, 3500))` |
| `axes` |  | str | `'xyz'` | Only move along these world axes; 'xz' keeps every height. |
| `rotation` |  | str | `'none'` | none; yaw: turn about the up axis so the from object faces along the world axes; full: turn so its whole orientation lines up with the world. Turns about the from= point. |
| `nodes` |  | list |  | Move only these hierarchies (their tops) instead of the whole scene. Example: `relocateScene("Hero", nodes=["Hero"])` |
| `selectedOnly` |  | bool | `False` | Move only the hierarchies of the objects given (the selection by default), as nodes= does. |
| `dryRun` |  | bool | `False` | Plan and check, but change nothing; returns what would happen. |

```python
relocateScene("Ground", from="bottom")
```

```python
relocateScene("Hero", from="Hero", rotation="yaw", nodes=["Hero"])
```

### retopoConstruct

Topology: make a live construct (patch, strip, stroke, bridge, sweep, cylinder or auto region) on the retopo mesh, or change one by id: its faces are regenerated from the new spec and settled on the reference. A construct whose faces were edited by hand since is frozen instead (left as plain geometry). Returns {mesh, id, faces, variants, sideCounts, frozen}.

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mesh` |  | str |  | Retopo mesh. |

| `id` |  | int | `0` | The construct to change; 0 makes a new one. |
| `edgeLength` |  | float | `0.0` | Edge length for counts left on auto, cm; 0 takes a fortieth of the reference's size. |
| `settle` |  | int | `40` | Live relax steps on the new points; 0 leaves them as generated. |
| `weld` |  | float | `0.001` | Reuse existing points closer than this, cm. |
| `timeout` |  | float | `10.0` | Seconds an auto region may take; 0 is unlimited. |
| `reference` |  | str |  | Reference mesh, connected so the topology tools resume on this pair later. |
| `create` |  | bool | `False` | Create the mesh if it doesn't exist (taking the reference's symmetry). |

### retopoPoles

The poles quadRemesh's edge flow would turn at with these options, without remeshing: where each one is and its valence (3 or 5). Move, add or remove them and pass them back as quadRemesh(poles=...). Also returns, per closed shell, what (4 - valence) over its poles has to sum to.

**Objects:** source

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `targetFaces` |  | int | `500` | Approximate face count. |
| `timeout` |  | float | `5.0` | Seconds before giving up with an error saying how far it got, leaving the scene as it was; 0 waits forever. |
| `targetEdgeLength` |  | float | `0.0` | Edge length, cm; overrides targetFaces when positive. |
| `adaptivity` |  | float | `0.25` | 0 uniform, 1 much denser where curved; painted point 'density' multiplies. |
| `useHardEdges` |  | bool | `True` | Follow edges marked hard. |
| `sharpAngle` |  | float | `40.0` | Also follow creases sharper than this, degrees; negative disables. |
| `symmetry` |  | str | `'off'` | off, x, y or z: remesh half and mirror, exactly symmetric. |
| `guides` |  | list |  | Mesh nodes whose edges are guide curves. |
| `guidePoints` |  | list |  | Guide polylines as lists of world [x, y, z]. |
| `pureQuads` |  | bool | `True` | All quads; false allows a few triangles and pentagons. |
| `resolveGaps` |  | bool | `True` | Finer where the surface comes close to itself across a gap (a ball in a pocket), so the gap isn't bridged; costs faces. |
| `seamless` |  | bool | `False` | Experimental: also try a global layout that only turns at the poles, kept when it has fewer irregular points. |
| `poles` |  | list |  | The poles the edge flow turns at, as {position: world [x, y, z], valence: 3 or 5}, and nowhere else. Start from retopoPoles; on a closed shell (4 - valence) must sum to what retopoPoles reports. |

Not undoable.

### sculptCorrective

Start a corrective: pose the rig, then this copies the mesh as it looks now into <mesh>_corrective, in place, and hides the mesh. Sculpt the fix on the copy, then run addCorrective. Returns the sculpt mesh.

**Objects:** mesh

### sculptEnter

Enter sculpt mode on a mesh: builds a temporary high-resolution proxy of its cage to sculpt on. mode='subdivide' (Catmull-Clark, levels deep) reprojects exactly on exit; 'remesh' sculpts a uniform voxel remesh; 'direct' sculpts the mesh itself. Resumes from a kept proxy when there is one. Returns {mesh, mode, levels, points, faces}.

**Objects:** mesh

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` |  | str | `'subdivide'` | subdivide, remesh or direct. |

| `resolution` |  | int | `192` | Voxels along the longest side, for mode='remesh'. |
| `resume` |  | bool | `True` | Continue from the mesh's kept proxy when it has one. |

### sculptExit

Leave sculpt mode, moving the low-poly cage onto the sculpt. method='fit' solves for the cage whose subdivision best matches the sculpt (least squares through the subdivision stencils); 'closest' and 'normal' project each cage point onto the sculpted surface instead. Only positions change: UVs and other attributes stay. keepProxy stores the proxy as a hidden child mesh to resume from. Returns {mesh, maxMove}.

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `method` |  | str | `'fit'` | fit, closest or normal. |
| `keepProxy` |  | bool | `False` | Keep the sculpt as a hidden child mesh. |
| `iterations` |  | int | `3` | Project-and-fit rounds for remeshed proxies. |

### sculptMask

Change the sculpt mask (masked points resist every brush) or the freeze layer (frozen points never move): clear, fill, invert, or blur (mask only).

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `op` |  | str | `'clear'` | clear, fill, invert or blur. |

| `iterations` |  | int | `2` | Blur passes. |

One brush stroke on the sculpt proxy: dabs is a list of {center, normal, radius, pressure, opacity, flow, view, delta, direction} in world space (only center is required; opacity defaults to pressure). Honours the mask, frozen points and the mesh's symmetry, mirrored exactly. Returns {points} changed.

### selectLoop

Extend the selection to full loops (or rings with ring=True): edges along their own loops, vertices along the loops of the edges joining them, faces along the face loops crossing the edges they share.

Select the edge loop (or ring) through one edge of a mesh, or with faces=True the face loop crossing it. Without add/deselect/toggle it replaces the selection of that kind. Returns the ids.

### selectMode

Switch between object, vertex, edge and face selection. With no argument, returns the current mode.

Not undoable.

### selectPathBetween

Select the components between two of a mesh's vertices, edges or faces: the shorter way along a loop or ring they share, else the shortest path across the surface. Neighbours (vertices on one edge, edges along a loop or across a quad, faces sharing an edge) select the whole loop or ring through both instead. Adds to the selection unless replace or deselect. Returns the ids in order.

**Objects:** mesh

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` |  | str | `'edge'` | vertex \| edge \| face |
| `from` |  | int |  | Id the path starts at. |
| `to` |  | int |  | Id the path ends at. |
| `replace` |  | bool | `False` | Replace the selection of that kind. |
| `deselect` |  | bool | `False` | Remove the path from the selection. |
| `symmetric` |  | bool | `False` | Also the mirror images, when the mesh's symmetry is on. |

Add or change a map of a bake project: on/off, file suffix ({map}), bit depth, format and options (normal: greenUp, flipX; height: range; id: source, palette; ao: rays, distance, scope). bakeMaps lists the maps. Returns the project's maps.

### setBakeOutput

Set where and how a bake project writes: folder, file name template (tokens {project} {group} {mesh} {material} {map} {udim} {res} {ext}; several groups share a texture when their names resolve to the same file), format, bit depth, resolution, supersampling and padding. Returns the output settings.

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `project` | `pj` | str |  | The bake project; defaults to the scene's only one. |
| `folder` | `fo` | str |  | Output folder; relative paths are under the workspace, else the scene file's folder. |
| `name` | `n` | str |  | File name template, e.g. T_{mesh}_{map} or {material}_{map}; .{ext} is added when absent. |
| `format` | `f` | str |  | png, exr, tga, tif or psd (one layered file per texture set, a layer per map). One of `png`, `exr`, `tga`, `tif`, `tiff`, `psd`. |
| `bits` | `b` | int |  | 8 or 16 (PNG, PSD); 8, 16 or 32 float (TIFF); 16 half or 32 float (EXR). |
| `dither` | `di` | bool |  | Triangular dither when writing 8 bit (never on ID or island maps). |
| `compression` | `cmp` | str |  | TIFF: deflate or none. |
| `compressionLevel` | `cl` | int |  | Deflate level for PNG, EXR and TIFF: 1 fastest (default 2) to 9 smallest. |
| `udimNaming` | `un` | str |  | How {udim} reads: 1001, uv (u1_v1) or uv0 (u0_v0). |
| `sidecar` | `sc` | bool |  | Write <texture>.json beside each texture (map, colour space, decode data). |
| `resolution` | `res` | int |  | Width and height. |
| `width` | `w` | int |  | Width in texels. |
| `height` | `h` | int |  | Height in texels. |
| `supersampling` | `ss` | int |  | Samples per texel: 1, 4, 16 or 64. |
| `padding` | `pad` | int |  | Texels of dilation past island borders; -1 fills the texture. |

### setProxyDisplay

Show anim proxies or the real meshes. Targets are proxy sets, or anything they stand in for: a real mesh, a piece, or a joint of the character (every set of its skeleton); every set when none are given or selected. Returns the display set.

With piece, only that piece's joint changes: pieceDisplay real shows its true piece (the real head for facial animation, say) while the rest stays proxy.

**Objects:** targets

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `display` | `d` | str | `'toggle'` | proxy, real or toggle. |
| `piece` | `pc` | str |  | A piece, or a joint whose pieces to override. |
| `pieceDisplay` | `pd` | str | `'real'` | follow, proxy or real. |

```python
setProxyDisplay("Body_animProxy", display="real")
```

```python
setProxyDisplay(piece="head", pieceDisplay="real")
```

### shrinkwrap

| `offset` |  | float | `0.0` | Distance kept off the target along its normal, cm; negative goes inside. |
| `maxDistance` |  | float | `-1.0` | Leave points farther than this, cm; negative is unlimited. |

Remove every sketch constraint and dimension from curves (the geometry stays).

### sketchCombine

Merge curves into the first one, so constraints can tie them together: their splines join it (kept where they are) and their sketch constraints come along. The others are deleted unless keepOriginal. Returns the first curve.

### sketchConstrain

Add a geometric constraint between a curve's points, lines and circles, and solve the sketch. Several lines for horizontal, vertical or fixed add one each; three or more refs for equal, parallel, coincident or concentric tie each to the first. Refuses a constraint that conflicts (naming what it conflicts with) or adds nothing. Returns the ids.

**Objects:** curve

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `t` | str | `'coincident'` | The constraint. One of `coincident`, `horizontal`, `vertical`, `parallel`, `perpendicular`, `tangent`, `equal`, `concentric`, `midpoint`, `symmetric`, `fixed`, `pointOnCurve`, `collinear`. |
| `refs` | `r` | list |  | What it applies to: "p0.3" point 3 of spline 0 ("p0.end" its last), "l0.3" the line from point 3 to 4, "c1" spline 1 (a circle, arc or any curve), "o1" a circle's centre, "hl0.3"/"hr0.3" Bezier handles. Default: the selected points. |
| `force` |  | bool | `False` | Keep a constraint even when it conflicts or adds nothing. |
| `planeNormal` |  | tuple[float, float, float] |  | The sketch plane's normal (object space) when the curve has no sketch yet; default its best-fit plane. |
| `planeOrigin` |  | tuple[float, float, float] |  | A point on the sketch plane, with planeNormal. |

Delete sketch constraints or dimensions by id; the geometry stays where it is. Dimensions others' expressions use leave their value behind in those expressions.

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ids` |  | list |  | Constraint ids. |

Add a dimension (distance, horizontal or vertical distance, length, radius, diameter or angle) and solve the sketch to it. Without a value it keeps the current measurement. expr makes it parametric: other dimensions by name (d1), units (mm, cm, m, in, deg), + - * / ^ and sin, cos, sqrt... Returns {id, name, value}.

| `value` | `v` | float |  | cm, or degrees for angle; default the current measurement. |
| `expr` | `e` | str |  | An expression for the value, kept live (e.g. "d1 * 2", "25mm"). |

| `bindTo` | `bt` | str | `'hierarchy'` | hierarchy \| selected |
| `skinningMethod` | `sm` | str | `'linear'` | linear \| dualQuaternion \| centresOfRotation \| directDeltaMush |
| `name` | `n` | str |  | Name for the skinCluster. |

| `name` |  | str |  | Name of the joined mesh. |

### splitMesh

Cut a mesh into pieces along planes, each cutting only within its disc, and optionally remesh each piece. Returns the pieces.

planes are world space: [{origin, normal, radius}], or {joint} for a plane at a joint facing along its bone. A radius of 0 fits the plane to the mesh's cross-section around its origin. With suggest, planes go where the joints a click selects meet on a skinned mesh. pieceSettings overrides the remesh per piece: {"2": {"remesh": "none"}}.

**Objects:** mesh

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `planes` | `pl` | Any |  | World planes: [{"origin": [x, y, z], "normal": [x, y, z], "radius": r}] or [{"joint": name}]. |
| `suggest` | `sg` | bool | `False` | Add planes at the joint boundaries of a skinned mesh. |
| `duplicate` | `dup` | bool | `True` | Leave the mesh and make the pieces from a copy; off replaces it. |
| `cap` | `c` | bool | `True` | Close the holes the cuts leave. |
| `mergeLoose` | `ml` | bool | `True` | Shells no plane cuts join the nearest piece. |
| `remesh` | `rm` | str | `'none'` | How each piece is rebuilt. One of `none`, `quadRemesh`, `voxelRemesh`, `decimate`. |
| `targetFaces` | `tf` | int | `300` | Quad remesh: faces per piece. |
| `resolution` | `res` | int | `32` | Voxel remesh: voxels along a piece's longest side. |
| `ratio` | `r` | float | `0.25` | Decimate: share of triangles kept. |
| `pieceSettings` | `ps` | Any |  | Per piece index: {remesh, targetFaces, resolution, ratio}. |
| `pieceFaces` | `pf` | str |  | Face count per piece, as index:count pairs (0:150 3:80). |
| `exactPieces` | `ep` | str |  | Pieces kept exact, by index (1 4). |
| `name` | `n` | str |  | Base name of the pieces; the mesh's name by default. |

```python
splitMesh("Body", planes=[{"origin": [0, 140, 0], "normal": [0, 1, 0]}])
```

```python
splitMesh("Body", suggest=True, remesh="voxelRemesh", pieceSettings={"0": {"remesh": "none"}})
```

### symmetrize

Make meshes exactly symmetric: every point on one side of the symmetry plane is copied, reflected, onto its partner, and on-plane points are put on the plane. With radial symmetry, one wedge's points are copied round the axis onto their orbits.

**Objects:** objects

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `side` |  | str | `'positive'` | The side that is kept. One of `positive`, `negative`. |
| `wedge` |  | int | `-1` | Radial: the wedge that is kept; -1: the one most of the selected components are in, else 0. |

### symmetrizeRadial

Rebuild meshes exactly radially symmetric: the kept wedge is repeated round the axis (and mirrored within each wedge with mirror=True), replacing the rest, and welded along the seams and the axis; then the mesh's symmetry is set to radial with these settings, so every edit after keeps it. Settings default to the mesh's own radial symmetry. Model one wedge and run this to get the whole. Returns the faces per mesh.

**Objects:** objects

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `count` |  | int |  | Radial: how many wedges repeat round the axis, 2 to 64; default: the mesh's own. |
| `radialAxis` |  | str |  | Radial: the axis, x, y, z or custom (direction=); default: the mesh's own. |
| `direction` |  | tuple[float, float, float] |  | Radial: a custom axis direction, object space. |
| `mirror` |  | bool |  | Radial: also mirror each wedge across a plane through the axis (dihedral symmetry). |
| `phase` |  | float |  | Radial: degrees the wedge boundaries and mirror planes turn about the axis. |
| `wedge` |  | int | `-1` | The wedge that is kept; -1: the one most of the selected components are in, else the one holding most of the mesh. |
| `tolerance` |  | float | `0.0` | Weld distance along the seams and the axis, cm (0: scaled to the mesh). |

### symmetrizeSelection

Add the mirror images of the component selection, on each mesh whose symmetry is on.

### symmetryCheck

Report how symmetric meshes are across their symmetry plane (or round their radial axis): the largest distance between a point and its partner's reflection (or its orbit's image), and the points without a partner. For radial symmetry also the unmatched point ids and the count the mesh fits best. Changes nothing.

**Objects:** objects

### symmetryRebuild

Rebuild meshes symmetric: the kept side is mirrored across the plane through the object's pivot, replacing the other side, welded on the plane, and the symmetry pairs are stored again. A mesh with radial symmetry is rebuilt from its kept wedge instead (see symmetrizeRadial). With pairsOnly, the geometry is left alone and only the stored pairs are matched again, by position or, for meshes that are no longer symmetric, by topology outward from the selected edge (which must lie on the plane; any edge for radial symmetry). Returns the points left unmatched per mesh.

**Objects:** objects

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `axis` |  | str |  | x, y or z; default: the mesh's symmetry axis, else x. |
| `side` |  | str | `'auto'` | The side that is kept; auto: the side of the selected components, else the side holding nearly all of the mesh, else positive. One of `auto`, `positive`, `negative`. |
| `wedge` |  | int | `-1` | Radial: the wedge that is kept; -1: the one most of the selected components are in, else the one holding most of the mesh. |
| `pairsOnly` |  | bool | `False` | Only match the stored pairs again, leaving the geometry as it is. |
| `topological` |  | bool | `False` | With pairsOnly: match by topology from the selected edge. |
| `tolerance` |  | float | `0.0` | Weld or match distance, cm (0: scaled to the mesh). |

### texPaintStroke

Paint a stroke into a texture set's paint layer (layer=, else the active one, else the stack's top paint layer, else a new paint layer). The stroke is a record: {mesh, brush (radius, strength, flow, spacing, falloff, roundness, angle, alpha, strokeMode line, lazyRadius, mirror...), payload {kind, channels {baseColor: [r, g, b], roughness: 0.3, ...}, blend normal|erase|add|subtract|multiply, mask}, occlusion, particles}, plus either space=surface with dabs [{triangle, bary [u, v], radius, pressure, opacity, angle}] or [{position [x, y, z], radius}] (object space), or space=screen with points [[x, y, pressure]] and view {width, height, camera | view + proj | viewProj + eye | eye + lookAt + fov}. Payload kinds: paint; direction (tilt, channel: normal, or another channel for a flow map); smudge (amount), blur and sharpen (filterRadius texels, amount), clone and heal (sourceOffset [du, dv] or cloneFrom [x, y, z]); fill (fillBy mesh|island|material|selection with at [x, y, z], triangle, material or faces; no dabs); project (image: a file path, {path, rect [x, y, w, h], opacity}, or {width, height, data}, through view; facingFade, colorChannel; no dabs); normal (normalMode bump|stamp, stampImage, intensity, channel). paint and fill take source {library id | graph | node type, values, resolution, scale} to paint a material's channels, and any kind tip {node | graph, values, resolution} for a texture graph brush tip. particles {kind drips|rain|sparks, count, length, size, spread, rate, seed} adds particle dabs. Each stroke is one undo step and is kept, so texRasterize can replay it. Returns {layer, stroke, dabs, pages}.

**Objects:** set [layer]

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stroke` |  | Any |  | The stroke record (an object, or its JSON text). |
| `layer` |  | str |  | The paint layer (its id). |
| `mesh` |  | str |  | The painted mesh; default the first using the set's material. |
| `payload` |  | Any |  | What the stroke writes, when stroke has none. |
| `brush` |  | Any |  | Brush settings, when stroke has none. |
| `points` |  | list |  | Screen points [[x, y, pressure]], when stroke has none. |
| `view` |  | Any |  | Screen view, when stroke has none. |
| `space` |  | str |  | surface or screen (default: screen when there are points). |
| `particles` |  | Any |  | Particle brush {kind, count, length, size, spread, rate, seed}, when stroke has none. |
| `id` |  | int |  | The stroke id the paint tool painted live under. |

### textCurves

Make text as curves (Maya's textCurves): closed Bezier outlines of each glyph, exact, in the XY plane with the first baseline on the origin. The curveText node keeps the text, font and layout live, so editing it updates anything built on the curve (a bevelPlus, say). Returns [curve, curveText].

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` |  | str | `'Lila'` | The text; new lines start new lines. |
| `font` |  | str | `'Inter'` | A font file, or a family and style ("Inter", "Inter SemiBold", "Arial Bold") among the bundled and installed fonts. |
| `size` |  | float | `10.0` | Em size, cm. |
| `alignment` |  | str | `'left'` | Where lines sit against x = 0. Justify stretches wrapped lines to the wrap width (or the widest line). One of `left`, `center`, `right`, `justify`. |
| `anchor` |  | str | `'baseline'` | Which part of the block sits on y = 0: the first baseline, the top, the middle or the bottom. |
| `wrapWidth` |  | float | `0.0` | Lines break between words to fit this width, cm; 0 breaks only at new lines. |
| `letterSpacing` |  | float | `0.0` | Extra space after each character, cm. |
| `wordSpacing` |  | float | `0.0` | Extra space after each space, cm. |
| `lineSpacing` |  | float | `1.0` | Baseline to baseline, in the font's line heights. |
| `textCase` |  | str | `'as typed'` | Changes the letters' case without editing the text. One of `as typed`, `upper`, `lower`, `title`. |
| `width` |  | float | `1.0` | Horizontal scale of the glyphs: below 1 condenses, above 1 widens. |
| `slant` |  | float | `0.0` | Oblique slant, degrees; positive leans right. For fonts without an italic. |
| `weight` |  | float | `0.0` | Grows each letter's outline by this much, cm (negative thins it). For fonts without a bolder weight. |
| `underline` |  | bool | `False` | A bar under each line, joined to the letters it touches. |
| `strikethrough` |  | bool | `False` | A bar through each line, joined to the letters. |
| `kerning` |  | bool | `True` | Use the font's kerning. |
| `mergeOverlaps` |  | bool | `True` | Join a glyph's overlapping contours so each area fills once (variable fonts overlap them). |
| `constructionHistory` | `ch` | bool | `True` | Keep the history node so its settings stay live. |
| `name` | `n` | str |  | Curve name; made unique. |

### textMesh

Returns [mesh, curveText, bevelPlus].

### textureFolders

Which project images the material editor's texture lists show. Globs relative to the project folder (the workspace root, else the scene's folder): `*` within a folder name, `**` across folders, a pattern without '/' matches at any depth, and a folder pattern takes everything under it, e.g. Textures/**, **/*_old.*, Saved. Empty include takes everything; exclude wins. Kept in the workspace's .lila/settings.json, or with scene=True in the scene, where each list overrides the workspace's. With no flags returns the effective lists, where each came from and both levels.

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `include` | `i` | list |  | Include globs; [] clears them. |
| `exclude` | `e` | list |  | Exclude globs; [] clears them. |
| `scene` | `s` | bool | `False` | Set the scene's override instead of the workspace's lists. |
| `clear` | `c` | bool | `False` | Remove the lists at that level (with scene, the scene falls back to the workspace). |

### toggleSymmetry

Symmetry off on the meshes if every one already has it on (on axis=, when given), else on for all of them. Non-meshes are skipped. Returns the axis set, or 'off'.

**Objects:** objects

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `axis` |  | str |  | x, y, z or radial to turn on with; default: the axis already in use, else the last one picked. |

### toggleVisibility

Toggle visibility (the H key). Defaults to the selection. Every object ends up the same: hidden if most were visible (a tie hides), shown otherwise. Returns the new visibility.

**Objects:** objects

### transferAttributes

Copy UVs, normals, color sets, positions or named attributes from the first object to the others, sampling in world, object, component (same topology) or uv space, by closest point or along normals. guided is for similar but different pieces anywhere in the scene: each target is fitted onto the source and its UVs are rebuilt from the source's islands (seams carried over, each island unwrapped and fitted onto its source island). live=True adds a transferAttributes modifier to each target instead of baking, so the targets follow the source.

**Objects:** source targets...

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `uvs` |  | bool | `True` | Every UV set. |
| `normals` |  | bool | `False` | Corner normals. |
| `colors` |  | bool | `False` | Vertex color sets. |
| `positions` |  | bool | `False` | Point positions (shrink-wrap the target onto the source). |
| `attributes` |  | list |  | Other corner layers by name. |
| `skinWeights` |  | bool | `False` | Skin weights, by closest point (point index in component space). Both meshes must be skinned. |
| `sampleSpace` |  | str | `'world'` | world, object, component, uv or guided. |
| `searchMethod` |  | str | `'closest'` | closest or normal. |
| `keepShape` |  | bool | `False` | Guided: keep each island's shape as transferred instead of relaxing it (trim sheets); islands that fold are still unwrapped. |
| `separateUnmatched` |  | bool | `True` | Guided: faces with nothing like them on the source become islands of their own beside the layout; off, they join the island next to them. |
| `maxDistance` |  | float | `-1.0` | Ignore matches farther than this (cm); negative is unlimited. |
| `flip` |  | str | `'none'` | Mirror the lookup across the source's x, y or z axis. One of `none`, `x`, `y`, `z`. |
| `sourceUvSet` |  | int | `-1` | Transfer only this UV set (0-7); -1 transfers every set. |
| `targetUvSet` |  | int | `-1` | Write the source UV set into this target set; -1 keeps its index. |
| `sourceColorSet` |  | str |  | Transfer only this color set; empty transfers every set. |
| `targetColorSet` |  | str |  | Write the source color set into this target set; empty keeps its name. |
| `live` |  | bool | `False` | Add a live transfer modifier (follows the source) instead of baking. Returns the modifiers. |

### transferShape

Move low-poly meshes onto a high-poly one (an imported sculpt): the same cage fit sculptExit uses. The first mesh is the high poly, the rest are the cages. Only positions change, so UVs and other attributes stay.

**Objects:** source targets...

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `method` |  | str | `'fit'` | fit, closest or normal. |
| `levels` |  | int | `2` | Subdivision levels the fit goes through. |
| `iterations` |  | int | `3` | Project-and-fit rounds. |
| `pinBoundary` |  | bool | `False` | Keep border points where they are. |

### transferSource

Set the source mesh of transferAttributes modifiers: connects its mesh and world matrix, and refreshes the target's stored world matrix (run it again after moving the target).

**Objects:** modifiers..., source

### trimCurve

Delete the stretch of a curve between the intersections around a point (or parameter): with other curves (cutters, default every other visible curve), in 3D or as seen along direction. A curve meeting nothing is deleted. Returns what is left.

| `cutters` |  | list |  | Curves to trim against; default every other visible curve. |
| `tolerance` | `tol` | float | `0.01` | Curves closer than this meet, cm. |
| `direction` | `dir` | tuple[float, float, float] |  | Intersect as seen along this direction (the view), for curves that only cross on screen. |

### twistDriver

Drive twist joints from another joint's twist about the bone: a twist joint under the upper arm or thigh counters its parent's twist (source = the parent), one under the forearm or calf takes the hand's or foot's (source = that joint). The default weight is how far along the bone the twist joint sits. Returns the drivers.

**Objects:** twist joints

| `source` | `src` | str |  | Joint whose twist is read; default the twist joint's parent. |
| `weight` | `w` | float |  | Share of the twist; negative counters it. |

Remove a mesh's skinCluster and its influence links; the mesh returns to its bind shape.

### unrealMap

Map a node to an Unreal asset so saving the scene re-exports and reimports it. Stored on the node in the scene: it follows renames, goes with deletes and duplicates don't inherit it. Static and skeletal mappings need a mesh under the node. Replaces any existing mapping for the node. An object set maps its members as one asset, exported together where they sit. kind meshSequence sends an animated mesh as a static mesh per frame (<contentPath>_000, ...; reimported in place, frames past the end deleted) and can point a Niagara mesh renderer at them; geometryCache sends it as one Alembic Geometry Cache; vertexAnimation bakes it to Vertex Animation Textures and sends the rest mesh, the textures and a material instance that plays them (sequence for the range, vat for the bake).
