| `skeleton` | `sk` | str |  | Skeleton asset to reuse, like /Game/Chars/SK_Hero_Skeleton. |
| `facing` | `fc` | str |  | skeletal and animation: x keeps the character facing +X as modelled; y turns it to face +Y, Epic's mannequin convention (default the unreal pref /facing, x). Mesh and animations of one skeleton need the same value. |
| `importMaterials` | `im` | bool |  | Create the materials Unreal does not have yet (default on). |
| `materialFolder` | `mf` | str |  | Where materials are looked up first and created: /Game/... or relative to the asset's folder (default Materials). |
| `keepMaterials` | `km` | bool |  | On reimport, keep materials reassigned in Unreal on slots that still exist (default on). |
| `importTextures` | `it` | bool |  | Import textures the materials use (default on). |
| `combineMeshes` | `cm` | bool |  | Merge every mesh into one static mesh (default on). |
| `autoCollision` | `ac` | bool |  | Generate simple collision when there is no UCX_ mesh (default off). |
| `generateLightmapUVs` | `glu` | bool |  | Let Unreal build a lightmap UV channel (default off). |
| `normals` | `nm` | str |  | import \| compute |
| `lodGroup` | `lg` | str |  | Static mesh LOD group, like LargeProp. |
| `nanite` | `na` | bool |  | Build Nanite data (default off). |
| `existing` | `ex` | str |  | reimport (default: keep the asset and its references) \| replace |
| `reapplyOptions` | `ro` | bool |  | On reimport, apply these options instead of the asset's stored ones. |
| `save` | `sv` | bool |  | Save the imported packages in Unreal afterwards. |
| `sequence` | `sq` | Any |  | meshSequence / geometryCache sampling, the exportMeshSequence flags as a dict: start, end, step, fps, scale, padding, worldSpace, recenter, applyModifiers, normals, uvs, colors (the playback range without start and end). |
| `niagaraSystem` | `ns` | str |  | meshSequence: Niagara system whose mesh renderer gets the frames, in order, as its meshes. |

| `splineType` | `st` | str |  | spline: actor (spline components, default) or landscape (landscape spline control points). |

### unrealMappings

Every node -> Unreal asset mapping in this scene.

Not undoable.

### unrealPlaceInstances

Send meshes to Unreal as one static mesh asset per instance source, placed in the open level: an actor per member referencing that asset, or one instanced static mesh component (ISM or HISM) for a large group. Placements are keyed by each node's linkId, given on the first send and saved with the scene, so sending a group again moves, adds and removes its actors to match, also after a rename or reopening the scene. Returns the plan, with each group's import and placement results when wait=True.

**Objects:** objects

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `folder` | `f` | str | `'/Game/Lila/Instances'` | Content folder the assets go in; each is SM_<source name>. |
| `mode` | `m` | str | `'auto'` | How members are placed: actors, ism, hism, or auto (actors up to threshold members, then hism). |
| `threshold` | `t` | int |  | auto switches to hism above this many members (default the unreal pref /instanceThreshold, 50). |
| `dryRun` |  | bool | `False` | Return the plan without exporting or contacting Unreal. |
| `wait` | `w` | bool | `False` | Block until Unreal has imported and placed everything. |

Not undoable.

```python
unrealPlaceInstances("Bolt", folder="/Game/Kit")
```

```python
unrealPlaceInstances(mode="hism", wait=True)
```

Returns {queued} or, with wait=True, Unreal's {assets, warnings, errors}.

| `parameters` | `pa` | Any |  | Instance texture parameter per map; defaults NormalMap, ORMMap, AmbientOcclusionMap, BaseColorMap, ... as Lila's Unreal materials name them. |

| `save` | `sv` | bool |  | Save the packages in Unreal afterwards. |
| `wait` | `w` | bool | `False` | Block until Unreal finishes and return its reply. |

Not undoable.

### unrealSendTextureSet

Send a texture set to Unreal: exports it through the Unreal preset (only tiles and channels that changed since the last export are rewritten and sent, unless all=True) and updates the textures and the material instance of the set's slot (MI_<slot>), set on the slot of every mapped mesh using it. Painterly and Toon materials become instances of LilaLink's stylised masters with their palette values; others need materialParent (or the unreal pref), else only textures go. The set then also goes on every save. Returns {queued, textures} or, with wait=True, Unreal's {assets, warnings, errors}.

| `useHardEdges` |  | bool | `True` | Edges marked hard always get a seam. |
| `keepSeams` |  | bool | `False` | Keep the seams already there. |
| `maxDistortion` |  | float | `0.08` | Split islands that stretch more than this when flattened. |
| `visibility` |  | bool | `True` | Hide cuts where they are least visible. |
| `merge` |  | bool | `True` | Merge islands back while they still flatten well. |
| `method` |  | str | `'split'` | split (hard edges, open to disks, split where stretched) or optcuts (Auto Seams 2: seams and distortion optimised together). |
| `distortionBound` |  | float | `0.05` | optcuts: stretch (symmetric Dirichlet excess, all islands) to get under. |
| `seamWeight` |  | float | `0.5` | optcuts: price of seam length against stretch; higher keeps seams shorter. |
| `resolution` |  | int | `1024` | Target texture size, px. Padding and margin are in its texels. |

### uvBff

Boundary First Flattening of the selected faces' islands: conformal, with the boundary chosen first. free keeps the boundary lengths (least area distortion), disk makes a circle, rectangle straight sides between four corners (the selected vertices, else the sharpest), polygon one straight side per selected corner. cones adds automatic cone points that cut the island open to cut area distortion. Islands keep their place unless pack=True or they had no uvs.

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `uvSet` |  | str |  | UV set; the current one (uvSetCurrent) when not given. |
| `boundary` |  | str | `'free'` | free, disk, rectangle or polygon. |
| `cones` |  | int | `0` | Cone points placed automatically (free boundary only); each adds a short seam. |
| `exactLengths` |  | bool | `False` | free boundary: bend rather than stretch to close it, so its lengths are exact. |
| `pack` |  | bool | `False` | Pack the islands into 0-1 afterwards. |

### uvPack

Pack the uv islands of the selected faces (or whole meshes) into 0-1 with padding for a texture size. Every selected mesh goes into one shared layout, or each into its own with perObject. Islands are packed by their real shapes, into the holes of other islands, with rotations, optional mirroring and stacking of identical islands; the densest of several island orders wins. Returns the density reached (percent of the used tiles covered) and the texel density. Runs on worker threads and can be cancelled from the progress bar.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `uvSet` |  | str |  | UV set; the current one (uvSetCurrent) when not given. |

| `padding` |  | float | `4.0` | Texels between islands, held exactly (the search never lets two islands closer). |
| `margin` |  | float | `-1.0` | Texels from the tile (or region) border; negative is half the padding. |
| `paddingMips` |  | int | `0` | Padding and margin survive this many mip levels: both are multiplied by 2^paddingMips. |
| `rotateStep` |  | int | `90` | Rotation step to try, degrees: 0 none, 90 quarter turns, smaller for more. |
| `angles` |  | list |  | Exact angles to try, degrees (replaces rotateStep), e.g. [0, 90, 45]. |
| `freeRotation` |  | bool | `False` | Any angle: each island also tries its three best-fitting angles (smallest bounding box) and their quarter turns. |
| `flip` |  | bool | `False` | Also try islands mirrored (the texture then reads mirrored on them). |
| `orient` |  | bool | `True` | Turn islands to their smallest bounding rectangle first. |
| `scaleMode` |  | str | `'normalize'` | normalize: even texel density across islands and objects (world space). keep: islands keep their relative uv sizes. lock: islands keep their exact uv size and are only moved and turned. |
| `normalize` |  | bool | `True` | Same as scaleMode=normalize when on, keep when off. |
| `stack` |  | bool | `False` | Islands with the same shape (within stackTolerance) share one spot. |
| `stackMirrored` |  | bool | `True` | Mirror-image islands stack too (the mirrored halves of a symmetric model). |
| `stackTolerance` |  | float | `0.002` | Largest vertex mismatch for two islands to stack, as a fraction of the island's size. |
| `tilesU` |  | int | `1` | UDIM tiles across. |
| `tilesV` |  | int | `1` | UDIM tiles up. |
| `region` |  | list |  | Pack into [uMin, vMin, uMax, vMax] of each tile instead of all of it. |
| `texelsPerUnit` |  | float | `0.0` | Pack at this density (px/cm) instead of filling the tiles; overflow spills into further tiles. |
| `effort` |  | int | `1` | Search effort 0-3: island orders tried per scale (1, 3, 6, 12). Higher packs denser, slower. |
| `timeLimit` |  | float | `0.0` | Stop refining after this many seconds (0 never); results can then vary between runs. |
| `workingResolution` |  | int | `0` | Search raster cells across a tile; 0 uses the resolution up to 4096. |
| `layout` |  | str | `'fill'` | fill: fill the UDIM tiles in order. groupTiles: one tile per group. groupRegions: one part of tile 1001 per group, sized by its area. keepTile: islands stay in the tile they are in. |

| `keep` |  | str | `'none'` | selected: the selected islands stay where they are and the rest pack around them. unselected: only the selection packs, around the rest. One of `none`, `selected`, `unselected`. |

### vertexColorBake

Bake a grayscale map into vertex color channels: ambient occlusion from the mesh itself, cavity (creases dark), curvature (0.5 flat, convex brighter) or a height gradient along an axis. The classic masks for game materials.

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |

| `contrast` |  | float | `1.0` | cavity and curvature: higher reads gentler shapes. |
| `axis` |  | str | `'y'` | height: object-space axis. One of `x`, `y`, `z`. |
| `blur` |  | int | `0` | Smoothing passes over the result. |
| `channels` |  | str | `'rgb'` | Channels to change: some of r, g, b, a. |
| `target` |  | str | `'auto'` | auto (the component selection, or everything without one), all, selection, or element (whole shells of the selection). |

### vertexColorStroke

One vertex paint stroke: dabs is a list of {center, radius, opacity, view, eye} in world space (center and radius required). Mirrors through the mesh's symmetry and stays inside the component selection. One undo step that stores only the changed corners. Returns {corners} changed.

**Objects:** mesh

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `colorSet` |  | str |  | Color set; empty uses the current one (made, white, when the mesh has none). |
| `blend` |  | str | `'replace'` | Blend mode. One of `replace`, `add`, `subtract`, `multiply`, `lighten`, `darken`, `blur`, `sharpen`. |
| `color` |  | list | `[1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0]` | Linear RGBA. |
| `strength` |  | float | `1.0` | Most the stroke changes a point, 0 to 1. |
| `channels` |  | str | `'rgba'` | Channels to change: some of r, g, b, a. |
| `falloff` |  | Any | `'Smooth'` | A soft select falloff preset name, "softSelect" for the current curve, or keys. |
| `frontFacesOnly` |  | bool | `True` | Leave points facing away from the view. |
| `paintThrough` |  | bool | `False` | Paint points hidden behind other parts too. |
| `mirror` |  | bool | `True` | Mirror across the mesh's symmetry when it is on. |
| `selectionOnly` |  | bool | `True` | With selected components, only they change. |
| `radialCount` |  | int | `1` | Copies of every dab turned evenly about an object axis; 1 is off. |
| `radialAxis` |  | str | `'y'` | The object axis radial copies turn about. One of `x`, `y`, `z`. |
| `dabs` |  | list |  | The stamps, in order. |
| `live` |  | int | `0` | Internal: adopts the stroke the viewport tool already applied. |

### viewportStats

The active viewport's last finished frame as the GPU measured it: {frames, gpuMs, aoMs, cpuMs, meshDrawCalls}. frames counts frames drawn so far, so two calls apart give the frame rate. Unlike measureView it times what the view really draws, components and highlights included.

Not undoable.

### voxelRemesh

Rebuild meshes as one closed, manifold quad surface from a voxel grid, whatever state they are in: closes holes, fuses intersecting and inner shells. For dirty scans and kitbashed blockouts; UVs are not kept.

**Objects:** objects

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `resolution` |  | int | `128` | Voxels along the longest side of the bounds, 8 to 1024. |
| `project` |  | bool | `True` | Pull the result onto the input surface where it lies close. |

### warp

Add a warp deformer with a from and a to handle at the meshes' centre: moving, rotating or scaling the to handle moves the points near the from handle. Returns [from, to, deformers...].

**Objects:** meshes

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `position` |  | tuple[float, float, float] |  | Where both handles start, world. Default: the meshes' centre. |
| `radius` |  | float |  | Falloff radius, cm. Default: a quarter of the meshes' size. |
| `params` |  | Any |  | {param: value} to set on each deformer. |
| `name` |  | str |  | Name for the deformer. |

### wrap

Make meshes follow one or more driver meshes (proximity wrap): each point binds to its nearest driver triangles. Give the meshes to deform first and the driver last; more drivers with drivers=. Returns the deformers.

**Objects:** meshes..., driver

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `drivers` |  | list |  | More driver meshes, up to 8 in all. |
| `maxDrivers` |  | int | `4` | Driver triangles each point follows, 1 to 32. |
| `falloff` |  | float | `2.0` | Triangles within this many times the nearest distance count; higher is smoother. |
| `smoothInfluences` |  | int | `0` | Passes spreading influences to neighbouring points. |
| `wrapMode` |  | str | `'offset'` | offset \| surface \| snap |
| `scaleCompensation` |  | float | `0.0` | 0 to 1: offsets follow the driver's local scale. |
| `name` |  | str |  | Name for the deformer. |

### xform

Query or set the transform of objects, in local or world space.

Sets every flag given on each object, or with query=True returns one value of the first object: pass the flag to read as True. Values are local to the parent unless worldSpace is on.

**Objects:** Transforms to edit or query; the selection when none are given.

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | `q` | bool | `False` | Return a value of the first object instead of setting. Pick it by passing one of translation, rotation, scale or matrix as True. Example: `xform("cube1", query=True, translation=True)` |
| `worldSpace` | `ws` | bool | `False` | Read and write in world space instead of relative to the parent. Rotation and scale queries stay local. Example: `xform("cube1", worldSpace=True, translation=(0, 2, 0))` |
| `translation` | `t` | Any |  | Position as (x, y, z) to set, or True to read it with query. Example: `xform("cube1", translation=(1, 0, 0))` |
| `rotation` | `ro` | Any |  | Euler rotation in degrees as (x, y, z) to set, or True to read it with query. Example: `xform("cube1", rotation=(0, 45, 0))` |
| `scale` | `s` | Any |  | Scale as (x, y, z) to set, or True to read it with query. Example: `xform("cube1", scale=(2, 2, 2))` |
| `matrix` | `m` | Any |  | The whole transform as 16 floats, column-major, to set; or True to read it with query. Example: `xform("cube1", query=True, worldSpace=True, matrix=True)` |

```python
xform("cube1", translation=(0, 1, 0), rotation=(0, 90, 0))
```

```python
pos = xform("cube1", query=True, worldSpace=True, translation=True)
```

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `space` |  | str | `'world'` | Axes to line up with. One of `world`, `object`. |

## Destruction extension

Available when the Destruction extension is loaded.

### addExplosion

Set off an explosion in a destruction: on its frame, pieces within the radius are thrown outward, hardest at the centre. Add as many as you like, at different places and frames. A mesh not yet cracked finer near an explosion gets smaller pieces around the first one that reaches it. Invisible: add your own flash or smoke. Returns the explosion's node in the destruction's group.

**Objects:** destruction (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `position` | `p` | tuple[float, float, float] |  | Its centre, world space cm. |
| `frame` | `f` | int |  | Frame it goes off. Default: the current frame. |
| `blast` | `b` | float | `2000.0` | Speed given to pieces at the centre, cm/s. |
| `radius` | `r` | float | `300.0` | Pieces this far away or more aren't pushed, cm. |

```python
addExplosion('Destruction', position=[0, 100, 0], frame=24)
```

```python
addExplosion('Wall', position=[250, 80, 20], frame=40, blast=3000, radius=400)
```

### breakApart

Break meshes apart like concrete, glass or wood, and (by default) simulate them falling.

Adds a geometry-nodes modifier to each mesh whose group (Fracture, Anchor Pieces, Rigid Body Solver) can be opened and edited in the Node Editor. The settings that matter (pieces, seed, impact, roughness, strength, blast, start frame) show on the modifier and can be keyed. The pieces touching the ground are anchored, so a wall stands until the impact. Several meshes break together in one simulation (their pieces hit each other) on a new Destruction mesh, with the originals hidden; add explosions with addExplosion. Colliders are meshes the pieces hit that never move or break. Returns the modifiers.

**Objects:** meshes (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `material` | `m` | str | `'concrete'` | How it cracks. One of `concrete`, `glass`, `wood`. |
| `impact` | `i` | tuple[float, float, float] |  | Where it's hit, world space cm. Default: the centre of the mesh. |
| `pieces` | `p` | int |  | Roughly how many pieces. Default: the material's. |
| `seed` |  | int | `1` | Another seed gives another pattern. |
| `blast` | `b` | float |  | How hard the impact hits, cm/s. Default: the material's. |
| `startFrame` |  | int |  | Frame it breaks on. Default: the start of the playback range. |
| `simulate` |  | bool | `True` | Simulate the pieces; False only fractures. |
| `anchor` |  | bool | `True` | Tie the pieces touching the ground to it. |
| `together` |  | bool | `True` | Several meshes: one simulation where they hit each other. False breaks each on its own. |
| `colliders` |  | list |  | Meshes the pieces hit that never move or break (the ground around a pit, say). |

```python
breakApart('Wall', material='concrete', impact=[0, 120, 15])
```

```python
breakApart(material='glass', pieces=60, blast=1500)
```

```python
breakApart(['WallA', 'WallB', 'Ground'])
```

### collapse

Make part of a destruction give way from one side to the other, like ground failing under structural damage. Its pieces hold still until the failure reaches them, rumble harder as it nears, then come loose and fall; anything standing on them falls too. The floor under it is lowered by depth so there's somewhere to fall. Running it again on the same part changes the settings. Returns the Collapse node.

**Objects:** destruction (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `part` |  | str |  | Which of the destruction's meshes gives way. Default: the one breakApart was run on. |
| `start` | `s` | float |  | Frame the first pieces fall. Default: the current frame. |
| `duration` | `d` | float | `60.0` | Frames for the failure to cross to the far side. |
| `direction` | `dir` | tuple[float, float, float] |  | Which way the failure travels (world space). Default: +X. |
| `rumble` | `r` | float | `2.0` | How far pieces shake just before they fall, cm. |
| `lead` |  | float | `30.0` | Frames of rumbling before a piece falls. |
| `raggedness` |  | float | `0.25` | 0 is a straight front; 1 drops pieces in any order. |
| `depth` |  | float | `3000.0` | How far below it the floor is, cm. |

```python
collapse('Destruction', part='Ground', start=90, duration=60, direction=[1, 0, 0])
```

### exportBreaks

Write where and when each piece of a destruction broke off, to time sounds and effects in Unreal.

One row per broken link, by frame: Frame, Time (seconds), X, Y, Z (cm, in the axis profile's space), Impulse (N s) and the two pieces (PieceB -1 for the ground). A .csv imports into Unreal as a Data Table (the first column is the row name); a .json is a list of objects. Returns {path, breaks}.

**Objects:** mesh or its destruction modifier (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `p` | str |  | The .csv or .json file. |
| `end` | `e` | int |  | Last frame. Default: the end of the playback range. |
| `profile` | `ax` | str | `'ue5'` | Axis profile of the positions: ue5, ue6 or generic (Lila's own). |

Not undoable.

```python
exportBreaks('Wall', path='Export/Wall_breaks.csv')
```

### wedgeDestruction

Bake several variations of a destruction, one per seed, as rigid vertex animation.

Sets the modifier's seed to seed, seed + 1, ... in turn, bakes each to <folder>/<mesh>_seed<n>, and puts the seed back. Needs a seed input on the modifier (breakApart makes one). Returns the bakes' file lists.

**Objects:** mesh (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `count` | `c` | int | `4` | How many variations. |
| `seed` | `s` | int |  | First seed. Default: the one after the modifier's own. |
| `folder` | `fo` | str | `'destruction'` | Output folder; relative paths are under the workspace. |
| `start` | `st` | float |  | First frame. Default: the playback range. |
| `end` | `e` | float |  | Last frame. |

```python
wedgeDestruction('Wall', count=8, folder='Export/WallVariants')
```

## Foliage extension

Available when the Foliage extension is loaded.

### addBladeDeformer

Add a nonlinear deformer to the selected faces (a whole mesh when no components are selected), one per blade or one for the whole selection, weighted so only the blades' own points move and their roots stay planted. Then randomizes the amount in low..high. Returns the deformers.

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `k` | str | `'bend'` | bend \| flare \| twist \| sine \| squash \| wave |
| `perBlade` | `pb` | bool | `True` | A deformer per blade; off, one for the whole selection. |
| `fromBase` | `fb` | bool | `True` | Anchor the handle at each blade's root so it deforms root to tip; off centres it. |
| `spin` |  | bool | `True` | Spin each handle around the up axis, so blades lean different ways. |
| `up` |  | str | `'Auto'` | Up axis: Auto follows the scene. One of `Auto`, `X`, `Y`, `Z`. |
| `seed` | `s` | int | `0` | 0 differs every run; any other number repeats. |
| `low` |  | float |  | Lowest amount; the kind's default range when not given. |
| `high` |  | float |  | Highest amount. |
| `bias` | `b` | float | `0.0` | Bias to top, -1 to 1, over the amount range. |

### bladeDeformers

The nonlinear deformers of a kind on the selection or the named nodes (meshes, components, handles).

**Objects:** nodes (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `k` | str | `'bend'` | bend \| flare \| twist \| sine \| squash \| wave |

Not undoable.

### bladeExtrude

Extrude faces into blades that remember how they were built, so randomizeBladeExtrude can vary each one later. Faces default to the face selection (a whole selected mesh means every face). Returns {mesh: [blade ids]}.

**Objects:** mesh (with faces=)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `faces` | `f` | list |  | Face ids of the one mesh given. |
| `thickness` | `t` | float | `1.0` | How far the blades grow along their face normal, cm. |
| `offset` | `o` | float | `0.0` | How much the blades narrow as they grow: the cap border moves this far inward, cm. |
| `localTranslateZ` | `ltz` | float | `0.0` | Extra growth along the face normal, cm. |
| `divisions` | `d` | int | `1` | Segments up each blade. |
| `keepFacesTogether` | `kft` | bool | `False` | Connected faces grow as one blade; off, every face is its own. |

The blades of a mesh: [{blade, caps, walls, points, root (world), thickness, offset, localTranslateZ, base: {...}}].

**Objects:** mesh

Not undoable.

A range around the extrude values the meshes' blades use now: their mean, give or take spread. Returns {thickness: [low, high], offset: [...], localTranslateZ: [...]}.

**Objects:** meshes (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `spread` |  | float | `0.3` | Fraction either side of the mean. |

Not undoable.

### deleteBladeDeformers

Delete the deformers of a kind on the selection, and their handles. Returns how many went.

**Objects:** nodes (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `k` | str | `'bend'` | bend \| flare \| twist \| sine \| squash \| wave |

### randomizeBladeDeformers

Re-roll the amount of the deformers of a kind on the selection (found from a mesh, a component, a handle or the deformer), biased up the mesh by where their handles sit. Returns how many changed.

**Objects:** nodes (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | `k` | str | `'bend'` | bend \| flare \| twist \| sine \| squash \| wave |
| `low` |  | float |  | Lowest amount; the kind's default range when not given. |

| `bias` | `b` | float | `0.0` | Bias to top, -1 to 1. |

| `spin` |  | bool | `False` | Also spin each handle around the up axis. |

### randomizeBladeExtrude

Give every blade of the meshes random extrude values in the ranges given. Each blade is rebuilt from its root, so running it again rerolls rather than stacking. bias 1 gives the high end of a range to the blades nearest the top, -1 to the bottom ones, 0 is pure random. seed 0 differs every run. Returns {meshes, blades}.

**Objects:** meshes (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fields` |  | Any |  | {thickness: [low, high], offset: [low, high], localTranslateZ: [low, high]}; leave a field out to keep it. |
| `bias` | `b` | float | `0.0` | Bias to top, -1 to 1. |
| `up` |  | str | `'Auto'` | Up axis for the bias: Auto follows the scene. One of `Auto`, `X`, `Y`, `Z`. |
| `seed` | `s` | int | `0` | 0 differs every run; any other number repeats. |

## Masonry extension

Available when the Masonry extension is loaded.

### masonryInfo

What a masonry wall is made of, and whether it is clean.

Returns the same stats masonryWall does (stones, courses, roles, stone meshes, trimmed, dropped, triangle counts, bounds), the current settings, and checks: overlaps (stone pairs intersecting by more than 0.01 cm, 0 when clean) and ok.

**Objects:** mesh or its masonry modifier (default the selection)

Not undoable.

```python
masonryInfo('MasonryWall')['checks']
```

### masonryShip

Send a masonry wall to Unreal's open level, instanced: each stone mesh is imported once as a static mesh with three LODs (worn, clean chamfer, plain box), and the stones are placed as one instanced component (HISM by default) per stone mesh per ground chunk, so streaming and culling work per chunk. mode='merged' instead makes each chunk's stones one static mesh with the same three LODs. The core goes as its own mesh carrying the wall's collision as convex UCX pieces; stones have none. mode='lowPoly' sends each chunk as a box shell with the stones and core baked onto it (normal, AO, curvature) and its own UCX collision, for background walls and HLOD.

With textures=True (the default) the stones also get a shared atlas: every stone mesh's worn LOD0 is baked onto its box into one normal, AO and curvature set, in uv0 of all three LODs (the tiling projection moves to uv1), and the textures go to <folder>/<mesh>/Textures. Slots: MasonryStone (LOD0), MasonryStoneFar (LOD1 and 2, which want the atlas normal), MasonryMortar (core), MasonryShell (low poly); Unreal finds or makes materials by these names, taking a Lila material's values when the scene has one. Instances carry custom primitive data 0 a stable random and 1 height up the wall (0 bottom course, 1 top). Sending again replaces the wall's chunks in place and removes the ones it no longer has.

Returns stats (stones, assets, groups, chunks, average triangles per stone mesh at each LOD, collisionHulls, atlasTexelsPerCm, shellTriangles, textures, bakeSeconds, removedGroups) plus, with wait=True, what Unreal imported and placed. dryRun=True returns the plan without baking, writing files or connecting.

**Objects:** mesh or its masonry modifier (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `folder` | `f` | str | `'/Game/Lila/Masonry'` | Content folder; the wall's assets go in <folder>/<mesh name>. |
| `chunkSize` | `cs` | float | `400.0` | Ground cell per instanced component, cm. |
| `mode` | `m` | str | `'hism'` | hism or ism: stones instanced per stone mesh per chunk. merged: each chunk's stones as one static mesh with three LODs. lowPoly: each chunk as a box shell with the stones baked onto it. |
| `collisionBands` | `cb` | int | `1` | Height bands the core's convex collision is split into (UCX), 1 to 16. |
| `textures` | `tx` | bool | `True` | Bake and send textures: the stone atlas (instanced and merged) or each shell's maps (lowPoly, which always bakes). |
| `textureSize` | `ts` | int | `2048` | Atlas or shell texture size, texels. |
| `backend` |  | str | `'auto'` | Bake backend: auto (gpu when there is one), gpu or cpu. |
| `material` | `mt` | str | `'generate'` | generate: instances of Lila's masonry master (M_LilaMasonry, built once, then yours to edit) per slot. none: materials matched or made by slot name. Or a material path to parent the instances to, which must have the master's parameters. |
| `regenerateMaster` |  | bool | `False` | Rebuild M_LilaMasonry's graph from this version of Lila, discarding edits to it. |
| `dryRun` |  | bool | `False` | Return the plan, placements included, without writing files or contacting Unreal. |
| `wait` | `w` | bool | `False` | Block until Unreal has imported and placed everything. |

Not undoable.

```python
masonryShip('MasonryWall', dryRun=True)['chunks']
```

```python
masonryShip('MasonryWall', wait=True)['unreal']
```

### masonryWall

Build a masonry wall along a line or loop: stones laid in courses, corners bonded, a mortar core behind them.

Give points= (a new mesh holds them as edges) or a mesh whose loose edges are the footprint. The wall is a geometry-nodes modifier around a Masonry Wall node; every flag becomes a keyable input on it, so change the wall later with setAttr on '<modifier>.<flag>' and check it with masonryInfo. Stones are instances of a few shared meshes with stone, course, role, face, random and variant attributes. Returns the mesh, modifier, group and stats (stones, courses, roles, stone meshes, trimmed, dropped, triangle counts, bounds). Lengths are cm.

**Objects:** mesh whose loose edges are the footprint (optional)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `points` | `p` | list |  | Footprint, [[x, y, z], ...] in cm; the wall stands on the lowest point, Y up. |
| `closed` | `c` | bool | `False` | Join the last point back to the first. |
| `name` | `n` | str | `'MasonryWall'` | Name of the mesh made to hold the wall. |
| `bond` | `b` | str | `'running'` | How stones are arranged. One of `running`, `stack`, `english`, `flemish`, `header`, `gardenWall`. |
| `height` | `h` | float | `200.0` | Wall height, cm. |
| `thickness` | `th` | float | `21.5` | Wall thickness, cm. |
| `cornerAngle` | `ca` | float | `30.0` | Turns sharper than this, degrees, are corners. |
| `stoneLength` | `sl` | float | `21.5` | Stone length, cm. |
| `stoneHeight` | `sh` | float | `6.5` | Stone height, cm. |
| `stoneDepth` | `sd` | float | `10.25` | Stone depth, cm. |
| `joint` | `j` | float | `1.0` | Mortar joint, cm. |
| `recess` | `r` | float | `0.6` | Mortar set back from the stone faces, cm. |
| `bevel` | `bv` | float | `0.5` | Stone edge chamfer, cm. |
| `wear` | `w` | float | `0.5` | Corner wear, 0 to 1. |
| `jitter` | `ji` | float | `1.0` | Wander and tilt inside the joints, 0 to 1. |
| `protrude` | `pr` | float | `0.3` | Push out of the face, cm. |
| `variants` | `v` | int | `6` | Worn versions per stone size. |
| `detail` | `d` | int | `0` | 0 worn, 1 clean chamfer, 2 plain boxes. |
| `seed` | `s` | int | `1` | Random seed. |

```python
masonryWall(points=[[0, 0, 0], [400, 0, 0], [400, 0, 300]], bond='flemish', height=250)
```

```python
tower = masonryWall(points=[[100 * math.cos(a / 12 * math.tau), 0, 100 * math.sin(a / 12 * math.tau)] for a in range(12)],
                    closed=True, thickness=40, height=600)
setAttr(tower['modifier'] + '.bond', 'english')
masonryInfo(tower['mesh'])
```

## OpenUSD extension

Available when the OpenUSD extension is loaded.

### exportMaterialX

Write Lila materials to a MaterialX document (.mtlx): each a surfacematerial with its shader and a nodegraph of image nodes (UV set as texcoord index, wrap as address modes, nearest filtering as closest), packed ORM/MRO maps split by a separate3 node, normal maps through normalmap (DirectX maps flipped to MaterialX's OpenGL convention), emissive and opacity from the base color's alpha. Unlit materials use surface_unlit. Settings MaterialX has no input for are kept on the material node for importMaterialX. Objects stand for the materials their meshes use; without any, the selection's, or every material. Returns the path, or with report=True {path, materials, warnings}.

**Objects:** path materialsOrObjects...

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `surface` |  | str | `'openPBR'` | The lit surface: openPBR (OpenPBR Surface, where the industry is converging) or standardSurface. |
| `textures` | `tex` | str | `'relative'` | How texture files are referenced: relative to the file, absolute, or copy (into <name>_textures beside it). |
| `selectionOnly` | `sl` | bool | `True` | Without names: the selection's materials; False writes every material. |
| `report` |  | bool | `False` | Return {path, materials, warnings} instead of the path. |

Not undoable.

```python
exportMaterialX("C:/out/props.mtlx", "Brick", "Glass")
```

```python
exportMaterialX("C:/out/all.mtlx", selectionOnly=False, surface="standardSurface")
```

### exportUsd

Export to a USD file. The extension picks the format: .usda text, .usdc binary, .usd binary (or text with format='usda') and .usdz, a package holding the stage and its textures. Objects default to the selection (or every root with selectionOnly=False); their descendants come too.

Defaults suit Unreal's USD importer: Z up, metersPerUnit 0.01 (centimetres), UsdPreviewSurface materials and UsdSkel. The stage has one root prim named after the file, its defaultPrim, with the exported nodes under it and the materials in a Materials scope. Transforms are written as translate, rotate (in the node's rotate order) and scale ops, or a matrix when sheared. Meshes keep their n-gons (triangulate=True writes the viewport's triangles), split normals, every UV set (as st, st1, ...), the current color set as displayColor/displayOpacity and the others as color primvars, edge creases, and a GeomSubset per material slot when there are several. Materials map to UsdPreviewSurface: a UsdUVTexture per map read through one UsdPrimvarReader_float2, packed ORM/MRO maps as one texture feeding occlusion, roughness and metallic, DirectX normal maps flipped to USD's OpenGL convention by the texture's scale and bias, emissive intensity as the texture's scale, masked and translucent opacity from the base color's alpha, each map's wrap as wrapS and wrapT (nearest filtering as magFilter and minFilter), unlit materials as their base color emitted over a black surface, and twoSided as doubleSided on the meshes using it. materialX='openPBR' (or 'standardSurface') adds the same material as a MaterialX network under outputs:mtlx:surface, which previewSurface=False writes alone. Meshes a meshCache drives write their points as time samples.

Joints become a Skeleton (bind and rest transforms) under a SkelRoot shared with the meshes skinned to it; skins write jointIndices and jointWeights (pruned to maxInfluences) and the mesh's geomBindTransform, in the bind pose. Morph targets become BlendShapes with their in-betweens; a mesh with morphs and no skin gets a one-joint skeleton of its own so Unreal imports them. Nodes parented to joints are written beside the skeleton, their joint's motion baked into them. Cameras write their lens, film back and clipping. Curves write as BasisCurves (linear or cubic bezier) or, for NURBS, NurbsCurves. LOD groups whose levels are plain meshes become Unreal's LOD variant set.

Animation is sampled every frame over the range and written as time samples, at the take's fps (timeCodesPerSecond and framesPerSecond) with the stage's start and end time codes. One take goes straight into the file. Several (takes='all' or a list of names) become a variant set named 'take' on the root prim, one variant per take with its own samples and its range kept in the prim's customData; the first take is selected, which is what Unreal and other tools play, and importUsd(take=...) picks another. splitLayers=True writes the geometry, materials and animation into sublayers (<file>.geometry, .materials and .anim) that the file composes. Returns the path, or with report=True the files written and the warnings.

**Objects:** path objects...

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `format` |  | str | `'auto'` | auto picks by extension; usda or usdc chooses the encoding of a .usd file. |
| `upAxis` | `up` | str | `'z'` | File up axis: z (Unreal) or y. Assets land the same way through either, as with FBX. |
| `metersPerUnit` | `mpu` | float | `0.01` | Scene unit of the file in metres: 0.01 is centimetres (Unreal), 1 metres. Lengths are scaled to it. |
| `materials` | `mat` | bool | `True` | Write UsdPreviewSurface materials and bind them. |
| `materialX` | `mx` | str | `'none'` | Also write each material as a MaterialX network under outputs:mtlx:surface: openPBR (OpenPBR Surface, the successor to Standard Surface that renderers are converging on) or standardSurface. One of `none`, `openPBR`, `standardSurface`. |
| `previewSurface` |  | bool | `True` | Write the UsdPreviewSurface network; False writes only the MaterialX one. |
| `textures` | `tex` | str | `'relative'` | How texture files are referenced: relative to the file, absolute, or copy (copied into <name>_textures beside the file). A .usdz packages them whatever this says. |
| `animation` | `anim` | bool | `True` | Write the animation as time samples. |
| `takes` |  | Any |  | Scene takes to write: 'all' or a list of names, one 'take' variant each. Default: the active take. Example: `exportUsd("hero.usd", "Hero", takes="all")` |
| `start` | `st` | float |  | First frame; the playback start by default. |
| `end` | `et` | float |  | Last frame; the playback end by default. |
| `normals` |  | bool | `True` | Write the split normals; False leaves them for the importer to compute. |
| `triangulate` |  | bool | `False` | Write triangles exactly as the viewport splits faces instead of the n-gons. |
| `maxInfluences` | `mi` | int | `8` | Skin influences per point, heaviest kept and renormalised (4 for mobile). |
| `deformOnly` | `do` | bool | `True` | Deform joints only (IK helpers and rig-only joints stay behind). |
| `atOrigin` |  | bool | `False` | Drop the exported roots' own transforms, keeping their children relative. |
| `children` |  | bool | `True` | Include the descendants of the given objects. |
| `worldSpace` | `ws` | bool | `False` | Bake world transforms into the meshes and flatten the hierarchy (current pose, no skins or animation). |
| `lods` |  | bool | `True` | Write LOD groups as Unreal's LOD variant set; False writes every level as a plain child. |
| `splitLayers` |  | bool | `False` | Geometry, materials and animation in their own sublayers, composed by the file. |
| `selectionOnly` | `sl` | bool | `True` | Without objects: the selection, or every root when False. |
| `report` |  | bool | `False` | Return {files, warnings} instead of the path. |

Not undoable.

```python
exportUsd("C:/out/hero.usd", "Hero")
```

```python
exportUsd("C:/out/hero.usdz", "Hero", textures="copy")
```

```python
exportUsd("C:/out/shot.usda", selectionOnly=False, takes="all", splitLayers=True)
```

### importMaterialX

Import the materials of a MaterialX document (.mtlx) as Lila materials, mapped as importUsd maps MaterialX networks: OpenPBR, Standard Surface, glTF PBR, UsdPreviewSurface and unlit surfaces with their image textures, UV sets, address modes and filters, normal maps and the constant and arithmetic nodes that fold to a value or one texture's channels. Documents Lila wrote come back with every setting. A material whose name the scene already has is left as it is. Returns the new material names, or with report=True a dict of materials, created, skipped and warnings.

**Objects:** path

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `report` |  | bool | `False` | Return the import report instead of just the names. |

```python
importMaterialX("C:/library/metals.mtlx")
```

### importUsd

Import a USD file (.usd, .usda, .usdc or .usdz) into the scene. The stage is opened and composed first, so references, payloads, sublayers and variant selections all resolve, and what arrives is the composed result.

Prims become nodes with their names and hierarchy: Xform, Scope and untyped prims transforms (every xformOp kind and order resolved; translate, rotate in any order, scale and pivot land on the channels as authored), Mesh prims meshes with their n-gons, normals, every UV set (st, st1, ... in order, then other texCoord primvars), displayColor/displayOpacity and other color primvars as color sets, other numeric primvars as mesh attributes, edge creases, holes left out and materialBind GeomSubsets as material slots. Cube, Sphere, Cylinder, Cone, Capsule and Plane are tessellated to meshes. Cameras keep their lens, film back, clipping and projection; BasisCurves (linear, bezier, bspline, catmullRom; periodic and pinned) and NurbsCurves become curve nodes. Invisible prims arrive hidden; proxy and guide prims are skipped unless purposes asks for them.

UsdPreviewSurface materials become Lila materials (Unreal's default lit) with their textures: packed occlusion/roughness/metallic textures as an ORM or MRO map, normal maps' green convention read from the texture's scale, emissive intensity from its scale, opacity from the base color texture's alpha as masked or translucent, and each texture's wrapS, wrapT and magFilter as its map's wrap and filter. Unlit materials Lila wrote become unlit materials. MaterialX networks (outputs:mtlx:surface: OpenPBR, Standard Surface, glTF PBR, UsdPreviewSurface and unlit surfaces, also from referenced .mtlx files) map the same way, preferred over a UsdPreviewSurface beside them: image and tiledimage nodes with their UV set, address modes and filter, normalmap, and constant, multiply, add, mix, extract, separate and convert nodes that fold to a constant or one texture's channels. What has no Lila equivalent (coat, transmission, subsurface, other node kinds) is listed in the report's skipped entries. Direct and collection bindings both resolve. Textures inside a .usdz are unpacked beside it. Meshes with time-sampled points get a meshCache deformer playing every sample (interpolated between them); a mesh whose topology changes over time keeps its rest frame.

UsdSkel skeletons become joints, SkelBindingAPI skins skinClusters with their weights and bind pose, BlendShapes morph targets with their in-betweens, and SkelAnimation keys on the joints and target weights. Time samples become keys (linear, or stepped on a held stage), and the stage's timeCodesPerSecond, framesPerSecond and time range set the scene's fps and playback range. Instanceable prims and PointInstancers are realized: each instance its own transform, sharing the prototype's mesh data.

Axes and units convert as FBX import does: a Z-up stage is read in Unreal's axes, a Y-up one as Maya's, and metersPerUnit scales everything to cm. Lights, point clouds and anything else Lila has no node for are listed in the report's skipped entries (lights and point clouds keep their place as transforms). Returns the new node names, or with report=True a dict of nodes, roots, joints, skinClusters, cameras, curves, materials, take, takes, fps, start, end, keyedCurves, instances, upAxis, metersPerUnit, skipped and warnings.

**Objects:** path

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `parent` | `p` | str |  | Parent the imported roots under this node. |
| `prim` |  | str |  | Import only this prim and what is under it, by its path in the stage ("/World/Hero"). |
| `skins` |  | bool | `True` | Rebuild skeleton bindings as skinClusters; False imports skinned meshes in their bind shape. |
| `animation` | `anim` | bool | `True` | Turn time samples (transforms, joints, blend shape weights, camera lens) into keys. |
| `setPlayback` |  | bool | `True` | Set the scene fps and playback range from the stage. |
| `materials` |  | bool | `True` | Create materials from the bound UsdPreviewSurface networks and assign them. |
| `loadPayloads` |  | bool | `True` | Load payloads; False leaves them out and lists them as skipped. |
| `variants` |  | Any |  | Variant selections before importing: {'set': 'variant'} for every prim with that set, or {'/prim/path': {'set': 'variant'}} for one prim. Example: `importUsd("chair.usd", variants={"modelingVariant": "Rocking"})` |
| `take` |  | str |  | For files Lila exported with several takes: the take to import (a variant of the root's 'take' set). |
| `purposes` |  | Any |  | Prim purposes to import: a list of default, render, proxy and guide, or 'all'. Default and render by default. |
| `report` |  | bool | `False` | Return the import report instead of just the names. |
| `select` |  | bool | `True` | Select the imported roots. |

```python
importUsd("C:/assets/kitchen.usd")
```

```python
importUsd("hero.usdz", report=True)
```

```python
importUsd("set.usd", loadPayloads=False, variants={"lod": "proxy"})
```

### usdStageExtract

Turn stage objects into plain Lila objects: each one moves out of its stage, keeping its place, modifiers and everything below it, and its prim is deactivated in the edit layer. Use it before adding modifiers or deformers that should stay live, since a stage's layer holds only their result. Returns the objects.

**Objects:** objects (default the selection)

### usdStageInfo

A stage's file, edit layer (mode embedded, file or sublayer, and path), the layers it reads, its variant sets with their selections, its payloads and whether they are loaded, how many prims have objects, and the warnings of its last save. edits=True adds the edit layer's text.

**Objects:** stage (default the selected one)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `edits` |  | bool | `False` | Include the edit layer as usda text. |

Not undoable.

### usdStageLoad

Load or unload the payloads at and below a prim of a stage, rebuilding its objects. The load state is saved with the scene. Returns {loaded: [prim paths]}.

**Objects:** stage (default the selected one)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `prim` |  | str | `'/'` | The prim, by its path in the stage; / is every payload. |
| `load` | `l` | bool | `True` | False unloads. |

```python
usdStageLoad("set", prim="/Set/Building")
```

```python
usdStageLoad("set", load=False)
```

### usdStageOpen

Open a USD file as a live stage: a usdStage node holding the composed stage, its prims built below it as objects. Nothing is flattened: variants, payloads, references and sublayers stay live. Edits to the objects are written as overs to the stage's edit layer when the scene saves (and before a reload or a variant or payload switch); the source files are never changed. File > Open and Import of a USD file run this; importUsd flattens instead.

Written: moving objects (with animation), hiding them, deleting them (the prim is deactivated), mesh edits, material assignments and edits, new objects under the stage, objects moved to another parent, joint poses and keys, new joints, skin weights, blend shapes and their weights, variant selections and payload loading. What can't be written is listed as a warning when saving. Returns the stage node, or with report=True a dict of stage, prims, nodes, materials, skipped and warnings.

**Objects:** path

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `parent` | `p` | str |  | Parent the stage node under this node. |
| `name` | `n` | str |  | The stage node's name; the file's name by default. |
| `editLayer` | `el` | str |  | Where edits go: empty keeps them inside the .lila, a .usda path writes them to that file, one of the stage's sublayers edits it directly. |
| `loadPayloads` |  | bool | `True` | Load payloads; False leaves them unloaded (usdStageLoad loads them). |
| `materialX` | `mx` | str |  | The MaterialX surface new and edited materials get beside their UsdPreviewSurface: openPBR, standardSurface or none. Empty follows the stage: OpenPBR when it already uses MaterialX. |
| `variants` |  | Any |  | Variant selections, written to the edit layer: {'set': 'variant'} for every prim with that set, or {'/prim/path': {'set': 'variant'}} for one prim. Example: `usdStageOpen("chair.usd", variants={"modelingVariant": "Rocking"})` |
| `setPlayback` |  | bool | `True` | Set the scene fps and playback range from the stage. |
| `report` |  | bool | `False` | Return the report instead of just the stage node. |
| `select` |  | bool | `True` | Select the stage node. |

```python
usdStageOpen("C:/assets/kitchen.usd")
```

```python
usdStageOpen("shot.usda", editLayer="shot_lila.usda")
```

### usdStagePrim

Every composed property of a stage object's prim, custom schemas included: {prim, type, schemas, instanceProxy, properties: [{name, type, value, custom, timeSamples, authored}]}. Values are usda text at the current time; long arrays are summarized unless full=True; relationships list their targets. An object inside an LOD level adds level, the level's variant.

**Objects:** object

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `full` |  | bool | `False` | Every value in full, however long. |

Not undoable.

### usdStageReload

Read a stage's files again, keeping its edits. Edits made in Lila are written to the edit layer first; the objects of the prims the files changed are rebuilt. A scene also reloads its stages on open when their source files changed since it was saved. Returns {stage: {reloaded, updated}}.

**Objects:** stages... (default all)

Not undoable.

```python
usdStageReload()
```

```python
usdStageReload("kitchen")
```

### usdStageSetProperty

Set a property of a stage object's prim, written as an over to the edit layer; the object updates to match. The value is usda text ("(1, 2, 3)", "[1, 2]") or a number, bool, string or list. An attribute with time samples gets a sample at the current time. A property the prim lacks is added, custom, when type gives its USD type ("float", "token", "double3"). Relationships take a list of target paths. Returns the property as usdStagePrim lists it.

**Objects:** object property value

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` |  | str |  | The USD value type, to add an attribute the prim doesn't have. |

```python
usdStageSetProperty("Chair", "xformOp:translate", "(0, 0, 50)")
```

```python
usdStageSetProperty("Chair", "studio:assetId", "CH_014", type="string")
```

### usdStageUpdate

Take in what other tools and scripts changed in the stages' layers: files changed on disk are read again and the objects of the prims they touch rebuilt. Lila does this by itself while idle. Returns how many prims were rebuilt.

Not undoable.

### usdStageVariant

Switch a variant on a stage, written to its edit layer. The prim's objects are rebuilt from the new selection. Without prim, every prim with that variant set switches. Returns {prim: variant}.

**Objects:** stage (default the selected one)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `set` | `s` | str |  | The variant set. |
| `variant` | `v` | str |  | The variant to select. |
| `prim` |  | str |  | The prim, by its path in the stage ("/World/Chair"). |

```python
usdStageVariant("kitchen", prim="/Kitchen/Chair", set="style", variant="metal")
```

### usdStageWriteShot

Write a stage's edits as a small .usda that sublayers the source, ready to open in Houdini or Maya or to sublayer elsewhere. Edits made in Lila are written first. Returns the path.

**Objects:** path stage (default the selected one)

Not undoable.

```python
usdStageWriteShot("C:/shots/sh010_lila.usda", "kitchen")
```

## PhysicsAnimation extension

Available when the PhysicsAnimation extension is loaded.

### assignPhysicsMarker

Make the joints rigid bodies: a physics marker on each, its shape fitted to the joint's dominant-influence region of the skinned mesh (a bone-sized shape without one), limits fitted from the animation range when the joint moves. Returns the markers.

| `shape` | `sh` | str | `'capsule'` | Shape. One of `capsule`, `box`, `sphere`, `convexHull`. |
| `fitShape` | `fs` | bool | `True` | Fit the shape to the skinned mesh. |
| `fitLimits` | `fl` | bool | `True` | Fit limits from the animation range where the joint moves. |
| `start` |  | int |  | First frame for fitting limits. Default: the playback start. |
| `end` |  | int |  | Last frame for fitting limits. Default: the playback end. |

## Puppeteer extension

Available when the Puppeteer extension is loaded.

### bankDuplicateTake

Copy a take as a new, inactive take named with the next free _NN suffix (Walk -> Walk_01). Returns its name.

**Objects:** take

### characterLabels

The semantic labels of a character's joints (pelvis, thigh_l ...), from its rig template or by name, as {joint: label}.

**Objects:** a node in the character (default the selection)

Not undoable.

### cycleSide

Cycle Side: give the opposite side of the selected joints their motion half a cycle later, mirrored. Key k of the n keys before the loop key takes the pose of key (k + n/2) mod n, so n must be even. Returns the channel keys set.

**Objects:** joints (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `axis` | `ax` | str | `'x'` | Axis the mirror plane faces. One of `x`, `y`, `z`. |

### cycleStep

Cycle Step: build the second step of a cycle from the first. The keys in the first half are mirrored (left and right swapped, centre reflected) half a cycle later, replacing any keys there. The cycle ends at the loop key, or end. Returns how many keys were made and replaced.

**Objects:** a node in the character (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `axis` | `ax` | str | `'x'` | Axis the mirror plane faces. One of `x`, `y`, `z`. |
| `end` | `e` | float |  | Cycle end frame when the character has no loop key. |

### exportTake

Write a take (its settings and curves) to a .lilatake JSON file. Layer blend chains are not written; merge layers first. Returns the file, the curves written and the channels skipped.

**Objects:** take

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `p` | str |  | File to write. |

Not undoable.

### importTake

Read a .lilatake file as a new take on its character (matched by node names without namespace). The take it was active for stays active unless activate. Returns the new take's name.

**Objects:** file

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `n` | str |  | Take name. Default: the file's. |
| `root` | `r` | str |  | Character root to put it on. Default: the file's. |
| `activate` | `a` | bool | `False` | Switch to the new take. |

### puppeteerBreakdown

Breakdown: key the pose at the current time part way toward the previous key (weight -1) or the next key (weight 1), for the selected joints or (all) every joint of their characters. Returns the channels keyed.

**Objects:** transforms (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `weight` | `w` | float | `0.0` | -1 previous key, 0 unchanged, 1 next key. |
| `all` | `a` | bool | `False` | Every joint of the selection's characters (of the scene with no character). |
| `time` | `t` | float |  | Seconds; default the current time. |

### puppeteerCharacter

Make a Puppeteer character for a skeleton: it finds the meshes skinned to it and the rig template it came from, and groups its rig elements, takes and poses. Returns its name.

**Objects:** root joint (default the selection's top joint)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `n` | str |  | Character name; defaults to the root's name plus _character. |
| `meshes` | `m` | list |  | Meshes, instead of those skinned to the skeleton. |
| `template` | `tp` | str |  | Rig template id, instead of the one the skeleton came from. |
| `poseLibrary` | `pl` | str |  | Pose library group instead of the template or root name. |

### puppeteerCharacterInfo

A character's root, meshes, template, pose library, rig elements, takes and poses.

**Objects:** character or a node in it

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `character` | `ch` | str |  | The character. |

Not undoable.

### puppeteerFootChannels

Roll, twist and bank reverse feet by degrees (or to them, with absolute), within each foot's limits (footChannels).

**Objects:** reverse feet, their chains or ankles (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `roll` | `r` | float |  | Roll: positive onto the toe (heel up), negative onto the heel. |
| `twist` | `tw` | float |  | Twist around the ball. |
| `bank` | `b` | float |  | Bank: positive onto the outer edge. |
| `absolute` | `abs` | bool | `False` | Set the values instead of adding to them. |

### puppeteerFootLock

Lock (plant) or unlock the key at a time on IK and reverse foot controllers (ikLock): a locked key holds the controller, and the foot or hand with it, until the chain's next key. Toggles without state. Returns each chain's new state.

**Objects:** IK controllers, reverse feet or joints in IK chains (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `time` | `t` | float |  | Seconds; default the current time. |
| `state` | `s` | bool |  | Locked or not; default the opposite of now. |

### puppeteerFootPivot

Move one of reverse feet's pivots (heel, ball, toe, inner or outer edge) to a world position on the sole (footPivot).

**Objects:** reverse feet, their chains or ankles (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pivot` | `pv` | str |  | Which pivot. One of `heel`, `ball`, `toe`, `inner`, `outer`. |
| `position` | `p` | tuple[float, float, float] |  | World position; its height is dropped onto the sole. |

### puppeteerIkChain

Make an IK chain (ikChain) from a start joint to an end effector, under the joint's character. Grabbing its controller poses the joints' rotations; there is no IK/FK switch. Returns the chain.

**Objects:** startJoint endJoint (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `startJoint` | `sj` | str |  | First joint. |
| `endJoint` | `ej` | str |  | End effector. |
| `solver` | `sol` | str |  | IK solver; default ik2BoneSolver for three joints, else FABRIK. |
| `name` | `n` | str |  | Chain name; default <effector>_ik. |
| `parent` | `p` | str |  | Node to put it under; default the joint's character. |

### puppeteerListCharacters

Every Puppeteer character with its root and pose library.

Not undoable.

### puppeteerLooker

Make a looker (looker) under the joint's character: the joint aims at it, blended by its keyable weight.

**Objects:** joint (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `aimAxis` | `aa` | str | `'x'` | Joint axis that aims. |
| `upAxis` | `ua` | str | `'y'` | Joint axis leaned toward upVector. |
| `upVector` | `uv` | tuple[float, float, float] |  | World up; default +Y. |
| `distance` | `d` | float | `50.0` | How far in front of the joint the looker starts, cm. |
| `name` | `n` | str |  | Name; default <joint>_looker. |
| `parent` | `p` | str |  | Node to put it under; default the joint's character. |

### puppeteerMigrateRig

Turn older Puppeteer IK chains, reverse feet and lookers into base rig elements. Chains that were in IK get their IK pose keyed as joint rotations at their keys, and the per-key IK/FK flag goes. Runs on its own when a scene opens. Returns how many elements were converted.

### puppeteerMigrateSpaces

Turn the scene's puppeteerSpace nodes (older Puppeteer scenes) into base spaces, keeping every key. Runs on its own when a scene opens. Returns how many were converted.

### puppeteerMirrorJoints

Mirror joints (and everything below them) to the other side, naming the copies by the side the joint's own name gives (arm_l to arm_r, LeftArm to RightArm, l_arm to r_arm). Returns the new roots.

**Objects:** joints (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `axis` | `ax` | str | `'x'` | Mirror across this axis: x mirrors across the YZ plane. One of `x`, `y`, `z`. |
| `behavior` | `b` | bool | `True` | Mirror behaviour instead of orientation. |

### puppeteerMove

Move transforms by a world offset. aim (sticky aim) turns each one's parent to point at the new position instead, keeping the bone's length. Returns the count.

**Objects:** transforms (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `by` |  | tuple[float, float, float] |  | World offset, cm. |
| `aim` |  | bool | `False` | Turn the parent instead of translating. |
| `keepChildren` | `kc` | bool | `False` | Leave the children where they are (rigging a joint's pivot). |
| `stickyAim` | `sa` | bool | `False` | Rigging: re-aim the parent's and the joint's orients along the bones. |
| `sticky2nd` | `s2` | bool | `False` | With sticky aim: the secondary axis lies in the chain's plane. |
| `keepDirection` | `kd` | bool | `False` | With sticky 2nd: the secondary axis keeps pointing the way it did. |
| `fullBody` | `fb` | bool | `False` | Joints in a character move by posing the whole body: their pins and locked hands and feet hold. |
| `autoPose` | `ap` | bool | `False` | With fullBody: the auto-poser places the unpinned body (UE5 Manny joint names). |

### puppeteerPin

Pin joints so full-body moves hold them where they are, or unpin them. With neither pin nor unpin given, toggles each. Returns the character's pinned joints.

**Objects:** joints (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pin` | `p` | bool |  | True pins, False unpins; leave out to toggle. |
| `clear` | `c` | bool | `False` | Unpin every joint of the joints' characters first. |

### puppeteerPole

Swing IK chains' pole by degrees (ikPole): the knee or elbow turns around the line from hip to foot. turn also turns the reverse foot or IK controller with it, so the foot follows the knee.

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `by` |  | float | `0.0` | Degrees added to the pole angle. |
| `turn` | `tu` | bool | `False` | Turn the controller with the pole. |

### puppeteerReverseFoot

Make a reverse foot (reverseFoot) on an IK chain's ankle, with Puppeteer's foot limits: a control on the sole that poses the leg and rolls the foot over heel, ball and toe, swivels on the ball and tips over its edges.

**Objects:** ankle or its IK chain (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `name` | `n` | str |  | Name; default <ankle>_reverseFoot. |
| `parent` | `p` | str |  | Node to put it under; default the joint's character. |

### puppeteerRotate

Turn transforms by angle degrees around a world axis. inherit keeps their children's world rotation, so only the selected joints turn. pivot center turns them around their common centre. Returns the count.

**Objects:** transforms (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `axis` | `ax` | tuple[float, float, float] |  | World axis. |

| `pivot` | `pv` | str | `'each'` | each (own origin) or center (their centre). |
| `inherit` | `inh` | bool | `False` | Children keep their world rotation (inherit rotate off). |

### puppeteerScale

Multiply transforms' scale. compensate (toon scale) keeps their children's world size, so only the selected segment squashes or stretches. Returns the count.

**Objects:** transforms (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `by` |  | tuple[float, float, float] |  | Multipliers along the local axes. |
| `compensate` | `cmp` | bool | `False` | Children keep their world size. |

### puppeteerSnapReverseFoot

Put reverse foot controls on the sole of the current pose with roll, twist and bank zeroed, or (align) level them with the pose moved into the channels (snapReverseFoot). The pose is kept either way.

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `key` | `k` | bool | `True` | Key the control's channels at the current time. |

### puppeteerSpace

Give a joint spaces to animate in (addSpace): its keyed space channel picks the parent (0) or one of the spaces, and its keys are read in that space. Returns the spaceSwitch.

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `spaces` | `sp` | list |  | 'world' or nodes to use as spaces, in order. |

### puppeteerSwitchSpace

Switch a joint to another space at a time (switchSpace), keyed stepped, re-keying its translate and rotate so it keeps its world pose there. Returns the space index.

**Objects:** joint (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `space` | `sp` | Any |  | 'parent', a space's name, or its index (0 = parent). |
| `time` | `t` | float |  | Seconds; default the current time. |

### stackerCopyKeys

Copy keys' poses (and the gaps between them) for stackerPasteKeys and stackerInsertKeys. Returns how many.

**Objects:** a node in the character (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `keys` | `k` | Any |  | Key index (0 first) or a list of them, as stackerKeys numbers them. |

Not undoable.

### stackerCreateKey

Make a key after a key, holding that key's pose, one gap later (the gap before it by default); keys after it move later by the same gap. Returns the new key's index.

**Objects:** a node in the character (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `index` | `i` | int |  | The key to follow. Default: the last key before the loop key. |
| `gap` | `g` | float |  | Frames after it. Default: the gap before it. |

### stackerDeleteKey

Delete keys with their timing: every later key moves earlier by the deleted key's gap. The loop key can't be deleted (turn the loop off first). Returns the keys.

**Objects:** a node in the character (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `keys` | `k` | Any |  | Key index (0 first) or a list of them, as stackerKeys numbers them. |

### stackerInsertKeys

Insert the copied keys after a key, with the gaps they were copied with (the first one gap after it), moving later keys along. Returns the new keys' indices.

**Objects:** a node in the character (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `index` | `i` | int |  | The key to insert after. Default: the last key before the loop key. |

### stackerKeys

A character's keys as the Stacker lists them: every key across its joints and layers, in order, with its frame, the gap to the next key (frames), its breakdown/extreme mark, and which is the loop key.

**Objects:** a node in the character (default the selection)

Not undoable.

### stackerLoopKey

Turn the character's loop key on (a key one gap after the last that mirrors the first, curves cycling) or off. Returns the loop key frame, or None when off.

**Objects:** a node in the character (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `state` | `st` | bool |  | On or off. Default: toggle. |
| `gap` | `g` | float |  | Frames from the last key to a new loop key. Default: the last gap. |

### stackerMarkKey

Mark keys as breakdowns or extremes (or clear the mark); marks move with their keys.

**Objects:** a node in the character (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `keys` | `k` | Any |  | Key index (0 first) or a list of them, as stackerKeys numbers them. |
| `mark` | `m` | str | `'breakdown'` | breakdown \| extreme \| none |

### stackerMirrorKeys

Mirror the pose at keys: left and right swap, centre joints reflect across the mirror plane. Returns the channel keys set.

**Objects:** a node in the character (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `keys` | `k` | Any |  | Key index (0 first) or a list of them, as stackerKeys numbers them. |
| `axis` | `ax` | str | `'x'` | Axis the mirror plane faces. One of `x`, `y`, `z`. |

### stackerNudgeGap

Lengthen (by > 0) or shorten the gaps after keys by whole frames, retiming everything after; gaps stay at least a frame. Returns the keys.

**Objects:** a node in the character (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `keys` | `k` | Any |  | Key index (0 first) or a list of them, as stackerKeys numbers them. |
| `by` | `b` | float | `1.0` | Frames to add; negative shortens. |

### stackerPasteKeys

Paste copied poses onto keys, in order, repeating the copied keys when pasting onto more. Returns the channel keys set.

**Objects:** a node in the character (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `keys` | `k` | Any |  | Key index (0 first) or a list of them, as stackerKeys numbers them. |

### stackerResetKeys

Reset keys to the character's bind or ref pose (any library pose), optionally only some channels. Animated channels are keyed; others just take the value. Returns the channel keys set.

**Objects:** a node in the character (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `keys` | `k` | Any |  | Key index (0 first) or a list of them, as stackerKeys numbers them. |

| `channels` | `ch` | list |  | Channels: translate, rotate, scale or attribute names. Default: all. |

### stackerSelect

Key indices for a quick select: all keys, the first half or the second half of the cycle (the loop key is never picked).

**Objects:** a node in the character (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `which` | `w` | str | `'all'` | all \| firstHalf \| secondHalf |

Not undoable.

### stackerSetGap

Set the gap (frames) from a key to the next: the key's span stretches to fit and every later key moves with the difference. Returns the keys.

**Objects:** a node in the character (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `index` | `i` | int |  | The key whose gap changes. |
| `gap` | `g` | float |  | New gap, frames. |

### walkCycle

Generate a looping walk or run for a character whose joints carry semantic labels (from its rig template, or UE5-style names: pelvis, spine_01, thigh_l, calf_l, foot_l, ball_l, upperarm_l ...). Keys one cycle into a new take, in place, from frame 0 to the loop key. Returns the take, frames and joints.

**Objects:** a node in the character (default the selection)

| Flag | Short | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `run` | `r` | bool | `False` | A run: shorter contact, a flight phase, the bounce inverted. |
